latest.title: When do e-commerce prediction models fail over time? cross-task evidence on temporal reliability and model maintenance
latest.abstract: Machine-learning models in e-commerce are often evaluated on randomly partitioned historical data, whereas deployment requires prediction on future observations under changing populations and information availability. We examine temporal reliability and model maintenance across four public dataset–task settings: late-delivery prediction among eventually delivered Olist orders, matched 24-h cart-to-purchase prediction in Retailrocket and Synerise RecSys 2025, and 30-day repeat-purchase prediction in Online Retail II. Sequential analyses restrict historical features, model updating, and recalibration to information and labels available at each prediction or deployment time. Random-to-future differences varied substantially: Olist showed pronounced deterioration, whereas the other settings showed smaller or qualitatively different changes. In the primary Olist XGBoost analysis, cumulative retraining improved ranking and modestly improved Brier accuracy, while sliding-window retraining improved ranking but worsened probability reliability. Cross-model, matched-exposure, and sensitivity analyses showed that maintenance effects depended on setting, period, model family, and design. Post-hoc recalibration did not provide a consistently reliable repair, and same-base calibration effects differed from net maintenance-policy effects. The matched comparisons do not identify causal task or duration effects. These findings support forward-in-time evaluation that assesses ranking, probability quality, label availability, and maintenance effects separately rather than inferring future reliability from offline performance or task identity.

latest.title: The Influence of Digital Marketing and Service Quality on Grade X Students' Decisions in Choosing Private Vocational School In Jambi Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Digital Marketing and service quality on the decision of tenth-grade students in choosing a private vocational school in Jambi, Medan. This study used a quantitative approach. The study population was 222 tenth-grade students of a private vocational school in Jambi, Medan, with a sample of 143 students determined using the Proportionate Stratified Random Sampling technique using the Slovin formula. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression using the t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that Digital Marketing had a positive and significant effect on students' decisions in choosing a school (t-test = 9.351; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Service quality also had a positive and significant effect on students' decisions (t-test = 8.085; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant effect on student decisions (F count = 70.668; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). This finding indicates that 50.2% of the variation in students' decisions in choosing Jambi Medan Private Vocational Schools can be explained by Digital Marketing and service quality, while the remaining 49.8% is influenced by other factors outside the study.

latest.title: Consumer decision in online processed-food purchase: income, price, and digital quality perception
latest.venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This study analyzes the association of consumer income with online processed-food demand through digital quality perception and perceived price on digital food platforms in Makassar, Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a cross-sectional online survey of 162 female household food decision-makers. Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling in International Business Machines Statistical Package for the Social Sciences Analysis of Moment Structures, with bias-corrected bootstrapping used to assess the indirect association. Findings Consumer income was positively associated with perceived price, but not with digital quality perception or online processed-food demand. Digital quality perception was positively associated with perceived price and online processed-food demand, whereas perceived price was not directly associated with demand. The indirect association was positive but not statistically significant. The model explained 56% of the variance in online processed-food demand. Research limitations/implications The single-city purposive sample and cross-sectional design limit causal interpretation and statistical generalizability. Future studies should use longitudinal, multisource, or platform-based transaction data. Social implications Reliable digital product information can support informed consumer choice and strengthen trust in developing-economy e-commerce. Originality/value This study provides developing-market evidence that platform-based quality cues are the closest correlates of online processed-food demand, while price plays a limited direct role.

latest.title: GREENWASHING AND CORPORATE LIABILITY IN INDIA: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE EXISTING LEGAL AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORK
latest.abstract: Greenwashing is when a company makes false or exaggerated claims, or uses a vague, one-sided or weak or limited substantiation to communicate environmental benefits. It can lead to a misallocation of sustainable investments, affect consumer decision making and erode confidence in corporate environmental reporting. This paper critically considers the effectiveness of India's law and regulation in combating greenwashing and holding companies liable. Uses a doctrinal approach with reference to the official and self-regulatory information described, the legal position is up to 31 October 2026. The study is based on the following: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Greenwashing or Misleading Environmental Claims, 2024, by the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA); Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Guidelines on Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) and Green-debt safeguards; Companies Act, 2013; Advertising Standards Council of India (ASC) green-claims standards; and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, as amended. The quantitative data suggests that there is a material enforcement concern – while 211 advertisements were investigated in 211 of which 211 required modifications in 2024-25, only 34 were investigated in 2023-24 and all these 34 required modification for lack of substantiation. This is an administrative review sample, and not a population estimation of greenwashing in India. The analysis reveals that India has taken a step beyond a voluntary approach, notably with the 2024 CCPA Guidelines and SEBI's BRSR Core regime. But the framework still has a number of drawbacks, and is spread across consumer regulation, securities regulation, corporate regulation and environmental regulati

latest.title: Beyond Rational Choice: A Behavioral Game-Theoretic Frameworkfor Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Since Behavioral Economics explains decisions through bounded rationality and mental shortcuts, it is necessary to incorporate strategic interactions into such analyses. This study develops an integrated framework for analyzing irrational purchasing decisions, which includes elements of Behavioral Economics, non-cooperative Game Theory, econometric analysis, and an integrated model of consumer behavior, the Consumer Irrational Utility Model (CIUM). The study employs a quantitative survey of personal care products consumers in the FMCG market, modeling a consumer and a seller as two players in a 2 × 2 non-cooperative game. The game is analyzed using best-response strategies, followed by the derivation of a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. The results of the game-theoretic model are then tested using Linear Probability Model (LPM) and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for estimation purposes. The results of the behavioral determinants, validated in the LPM and WLS estimations, are then incorporated into CIUM, which explains how irrational behavior by a consumer deviates from the utility-maximizing behavior of a rational human being. The study reveals that in the Indian FMCG market, consumers mainly adopt the Relative Decision Paradox strategy, whereas sellers mainly adopt the Strategized Pricing strategy. The study further reveals that the behavioral variables identified in the study have a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Also, results from the CIUM indicate that the economic utility of a product and the utility influenced by various behavioral factors in strategic interactions in the market jointly determine the overall utility of a product for a consumer.

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: Promotions and Online Customer Reviews as Determinants of Purchase Decisions on the Shopee Marketplace
latest.abstract: The development of digital technology in Indonesia has transformed people's behavior, particularly in online shopping activities, especially through the Shopee marketplace. This study aims to examine the effects of promotion and online customer reviews on purchasing decisions, both separately and jointly. The research method used is a quantitative, explanatory approach. The subjects of this study are students of the Faculty of Economics and Business, University of Jember, who actively use Shopee. The sample was determined using a non-probability purposive sampling technique with 112 respondents. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS 31. The results show that promotion has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, and online customer reviews also have a positive and significant effect. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect with an adjusted R-squared value of 54%. These findings confirm that promotion and customer reviews are important factors in purchasing decisions on Shopee, particularly among students who are critical and selective in processing information before making transactions.

latest.title: CONSUMER EVALUATIONS OF RESTAURANTS IN BOLU ON DIGITAL PLATFORMS: THE TRIPADVISOR CASE
latest.abstract: This study examines user reviews of restaurants in Bolu on Tripadvisor. The research uses a qualitative approach and employs descriptive content analysis as the analytical method. A total of 274 user reviews from 10 restaurants that provided meaningful content and were posted between January and December 2025 were analyzed. The findings indicate that most reviews were positive, with taste being the most frequently emphasized dimension. Analyses of food and beverage offerings confirm the meat-based nature of Bolu cuisine, while local dishes such as mantı, gözleme, and soups strongly reflect the region’s gastronomic identity on digital platforms. Additionally, staff and service quality, atmosphere and ambiance, cleanliness and hygiene, and price–value perception were identified as key themes shaping the user experience. Overall, the results support the influence of digital user evaluations on restaurant image and consumer preference decisions, and demonstrate that both product quality and service performance in gastronomic destinations are perceived and evaluated through online platforms.

latest.title: Why Does Gamification Fail? The Impact Mechanisms of Gamification Design Flaws on Consumers' Continuous Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approach to uncover the influence mechanisms of gamification design flaws. In Study 1, we collected 24,749 consumer comments describing negative experiences with gamified shopping festivals. By combining BERTopic modeling with a human‐LLM collaboration, we identified seven latent concepts. Further analysis grounded in psychological reactance theory and affective events theory indicated that four gamification design flaws, namely narrative rhythm disruption, game interaction complexity, reward value distortion, and gameplay replaceability, affect consumers' continuous purchase intention through perceived manipulation and frustration. In Study 2, we collected survey responses from 398 consumers who participated in the gamified shopping festivals and used PLS‐SEM to test the proposed hypotheses. This research deepens understanding of the adverse side of gamification, contributes to theoretical perspectives on the mechanisms of gamification design flaws, and provides novel insights for optimizing gamification in e‐commerce platforms.

latest.title: The Effect of Service Quality and Digitalization of Betang Mobile Banking on Customer Loyalty Through Customer Satisfaction at PT. Bank Kalteng Sub-Branch of Bahaur
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of service quality on customer loyalty and the moderating role of banking digitalization through the Betang Mobile application at PT Bank Kalteng, Bahaur Sub-Branch. The study was motivated by increasing competition in the banking industry during the digital era and inconsistent findings from previous research regarding the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty. An explanatory quantitative research design was employed. The study involved 96 customers, with the sample size determined using the Lemeshow formula and participants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS version 4.1.1. The results indicated that service quality had a positive and statistically significant effect on customer loyalty (β = 0.328; t = 4.439; p < 0.001). Furthermore, banking digitalization positively and significantly moderated the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty (interaction coefficient β = 0.098; t = 2.193; p = 0.028), indicating that digitalization strengthened this relationship. The structural model explained 63.8% of the variance in customer loyalty (R² = 0.638). Reliability emerged as the strongest indicator of service quality, while repeat usage was the most prominent indicator of customer loyalty. These findings suggest that reliable banking services, supported by digital service innovations, can contribute to stronger customer loyalty and encourage continued use of banking services. Therefore, PT Bank Kalteng should prioritize improvements in service reliability while continuously enhancing the functionality, accessibility, and user experience of the Betang Mobile applicat

latest.title: Religiosity and consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z: does gender make a difference?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how religiosity is associated with consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z in a highly religious emerging market. It proposes the spiritual cognitive consumption theory (SCCT), a dual pathway framework, and provides preliminary empirical support for its overall predictive validity. However, these two pathways were not directly measured; future experimental research is needed to isolate each mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 Nigerian respondents were analysed using structural equation modelling. Gender significantly moderates this relationship: women tend to show a stronger association between religiosity and relational aspects (e.g. brand trust, emotional congruity), whereas men focus more on instrumental outcomes (e.g. product functionality, religious symbolism). Findings The SCCT framework provides a nuanced understanding of the tension between spiritual devotion and market-based consumption. The findings offer marketers gender-sensitive, faith-conscious strategies and position SCCT as a robust theoretical tool for understanding spirituality, cognition and consumption in evolving digital economies. Social implications The study contributes to sustainable development goal (SDG) 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by providing insights into inclusive, faith-sensitive marketing practices in the Global South. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the development of the SCCT framework, which integrates spirituality, cognition and consumption into a dual pathway model. This offers a novel theoretical lens for understanding consumer behaviour in religious emerging markets.

latest.title: The Effect Of Product Differentiation And Promotion On Purchase Decisions Through Purchase Interest As An Intervening Variable (A Study On East Asian Drug Stores)
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
latest.abstract: East Asia Drugstore in Medan City, which is known for providing traditional Chinese medicine and health consultation services, is facing declining consumer purchasing interest due to fierce competition from modern pharmacies. Contributing factors include a lack of product differentiation, innovation, and effective promotion, resulting in products appearing monotonous and unattractive. This situation reduces transaction frequency and customer loyalty, even though the demand for quality medications remains high. Increasing purchasing interest through product innovation, differentiation, and appropriate promotional strategies is key for stores to retain and attract customers. This study took the population of all consumers of the Eastern Drug Store, the number of which is not known with certainty, so the Lemeshow formula was used to determine the number of samples. The sampling method applied was accidental sampling, where respondents were selected randomly based on their availability and willingness to participate. Based on these calculations, the number of samples used in this study was 96 people. The results of the study indicate that product differentiation, promotion, and purchase intention have a significant influence on consumer purchasing decisions at the East Asia Drug Store in Medan. These findings can serve as a reference for other researchers to develop further research by adding additional variables, while also helping consumers understand the influence of products and promotions on their purchasing decisions. For the East Asia Drug Store, this study emphasizes the importance of increasing product variety, promotional strategies, and factors that increase purchase intention to strengthen competitiveness, while future researchers are advised to explore other as

latest.title: Building consumer–brand relationships in omni-channel retailing: AI personalization, relationship marketing, satisfaction, trust, and data privacy concerns
latest.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming customer relationship management by enabling personalized and seamless interactions across multiple channels. However, it remains unclear whether AI-based personalization can build customer relationships as effectively as traditional relationship marketing. This study examines the effects of AI-Driven Personalization (AIDP) and Traditional Relationship Marketing (TRM) on Customer Retention (CR), while exploring the mediating roles of Customer Satisfaction (CS) and Customer Trust (CT) and the moderating role of Data Privacy Concerns (DPC). Using a positivist philosophy and deductive approach, data were collected from 407 Omni-channel customers in Pakistan and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings show that both AIDP and TRM significantly enhance customer satisfaction and trust, which subsequently strengthen retention. Customer satisfaction also positively influences trust, while trust emerges as the strongest predictor of retention. Moreover, Data Privacy Concerns significantly moderate the trust–retention relationship, demonstrating that customers’ perceptions of how their personal information is handled can shape their trust. The study integrates technological and relational approaches within relationship marketing theory in an Omni-channel context.

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: Adaptive Decision-Making in Action: Decision-Maker Profiles Under Time Pressure and Incomplete Information
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: Competitive intelligence increasingly requires decision-makers to extract actionable signals from abundant, incomplete, and rapidly changing information within compressed timeframes. Although decision research has extensively examined analytical and intuitive reasoning, less is known about how these modes combine into distinct person-level configurations. Using survey data from 246 employees and a person-centred analytical approach, K-means clustering based on Analytical Orientation, Intuitive Orientation, and Contextual Adaptability identified four distinct profiles: an Analysis-Dominant Profile, an Intuition-Dominant Profile, a Context-Adaptive Profile, and an Analytical–Intuitive Integrative Profile. External validation revealed a significant Profile × Analytical Burden interaction, LR χ²(3) = 29.00, p < .001, indicating that the association between Analytical Burden and negative responses to time pressure differed across profiles. The study develops the concept of Adaptive Decision-Making in Action, defined as the capability to maintain, switch, substitute, or integrate analytical and intuitive reasoning according to situational demands. The findings extend CI research beyond the analytical-intuitive dichotomy by showing that decision-making may take distinct configurational forms and suggest that decision development should focus on the adaptive use of decision modes rather than on a single preferred style.

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: What shared responses reveal about audience behavior: neural prediction and the emerging potential of peripheral synchrony
latest.abstract: Predicting audience responses to dynamic media remains a significant challenge in neuromarketing and neuroforecasting. Intersubject correlation (ISC) has been proposed to address this need by quantifying the temporal similarity of neural, physiological, and behavioral responses among individuals exposed to the same stimulus. This narrative mini-review examines how ISC relates to preferences, judgments, and behavior and proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting its predictive value. Across modalities, ISC consistently reflects shared stimulus processing and is associated with attention, alongside additional links to engagement, memory, and higher-order narrative processing. Neural ISC has shown associations with individual, group, and population-level outcomes, although findings vary by neural modality, analytic approach, and behavioral endpoint. Peripheral ISC derived from gaze, heart rate, electrodermal activity, and facial expressions provides complementary information about interindividual alignment, but direct evidence for predicting consumer outcomes remains limited. At the same time, neural and peripheral measures capture various aspects of shared response dynamics, and combining them in a multimodal ISC approach may help distinguish synchronization in different functional domains, including perceptual, attentional, autonomic, affective, and valuation-related processes, and clarify their relationship to the target outcome. The proposed framework therefore conceptualizes ISC as a probabilistic predictor whose predictive value depends on which functional processes underlie the observed synchrony and their relevance to the specific outcome of interest.

latest.title: When does controversy discourse correspond to visitor demand? Discursive political consumerism in cultural tourism
latest.abstract: Online controversy discourse around cultural institutions is increasingly visible, yet whether such discourse corresponds to measurable variation in visitor demand remains unclear. This study examines how controversy-discourse frames correspond to visitor demand at the British Museum across two sustained controversies that differ in the degree and locus of institutional actionability: fossil-fuel sponsorship and contested cultural artefacts. Drawing on discursive political consumerism and the moral economy of visiting, we construct engagement-weighted controversy-discourse signals from 2.14 million posts across six major London cultural institutions and link them to weekly British Museum arrivals and monthly attendance for all six institutions. A monthly fixed-effects panel provides the main estimates, complemented by supplementary weekly analyses. At the British Museum, fossil-fuel sponsorship discourse is positively associated with aggregate institutional attendance, whereas contested-artefact discourse is negatively associated but more specification-sensitive. Because the two signals overlap, the frame-specific interpretation remains tentative. Weekly models do not detect a robust short-run arrivals response. The study advances political-consumerism research in cultural tourism by providing a human-validated, frame-differentiated account of associations between public controversy discourse and aggregate institutional attendance. For heritage managers, the findings support assessing controversy discourse alongside attendance, visitor feedback and the institution’s capacity to address sponsorship or restitution claims.

latest.title: How recommendation explanation cues shape consumers’ multistage online behavior: An integrative information-processing framework
latest.abstract: 摘要： 算法推荐已成为电商平台影响消费者决策的重要信息环境, 但既有研究侧重算法类型、准确性及转化效果, 较少考察推荐解释线索对消费者信息加工与多阶段决策的影响。本文聚焦前端的相似用户型与产品属性型解释线索, 将其视为具有不同心理含义的信息线索, 而非后台算法类型: 前者强调相似他人行为, 后者强调产品属性匹配, 并构建购前搜索—购中选择—购后反馈框架。购前, 产品属性型线索通过降低感知产品差异促进目标导向型搜索; 相似用户型线索通过提高感知产品差异促进探索型搜索。购中, 相似用户型线索借助社会证明降低感知产品不确定性, 提高选择不熟悉产品的可能性, 增强选择信心并提升决策效率。购后, 相似用户型线索形成的推荐来源表征通过增强产品社会联结感, 提高反馈努力与质量, 并可能在后续评价触点中被重新激活。本文揭示推荐解释线索通过差异化信息加工机制影响消费者在线多阶段行为, 为推荐解释设计与消费者信息加工研究提供整合框架。

latest.title: Pengaruh Social Media Marketing terhadap Purchase Intention dengan Brand Image dan Brand Awareness sebagai Mediasi pada Produk Kosmetik Hanasui
latest.venue: CEMERLANG Jurnal Manajemen dan Ekonomi Bisnis
latest.abstract: The rapid digitalization of the cosmetics industry has significantly shifted the shopping behavior of Generation Z, making TikTok a highly strategic social media marketing platform. This research aims to examine the impact of social media marketing on purchase intention for Hanasui cosmetic products in Tangerang Regency, incorporating brand image and brand awareness as mediating variables. Employing a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected through purposive sampling from 110 active TikTok users aged 17 to 27 years old. The empirical data were then analyzed using the Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method via SmartPLS software. The findings reveal that social media marketing has a positive and significant direct effect on brand image, brand awareness, and purchase intention. Furthermore, both brand image and brand awareness positively influence purchase intention and serve as significant mediators in the relationship between social media marketing and purchase intention. Practically, this study suggests that cosmetics companies should develop interactive and engaging digital content to strengthen brand familiarity and positive impressions, which effectively stimulates consumers' purchase intentions.

latest.title: Green nudges for sustainable e-commerce: a bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: In view of the rising online consumption and growing environmental concerns, e-commerce platforms face a critical dilemma. They need to influence consumer choices toward sustainability without compromising user autonomy or crossing ethical boundaries. Incorporating green nudges—subtle design prompts intended to steer users toward more eco-friendly decisions—has emerged as a promising yet controversial strategy. This study conducts a systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, to examine how green nudges are used in digital commerce and how effective they are in promoting sustainable purchasing patterns. A comprehensive Scopus search of studies on green nudging in e-commerce reveals a 28.21% annual publication growth rate and an average of 25.68 citations across 33 countries. Bibliometric and content analysis reveals emerging themes and identifies the contextual factors that shape the success of these interventions. The findings highlight the potential of green nudges but also reveal key challenges, including inconsistent implementation, culturally variable outcomes, and ethical concerns about manipulation. The review underscores the need for a more nuanced, context-sensitive approach to green nudge design, accounting for user demographics, digital architecture, and behavioral science. This work both synthesizes current knowledge and proposes a research agenda to guide ethical and effective use of green nudges in sustainable e-commerce.

latest.title: Attitudes, Emotions, and Socially Responsible Identity Among Generation Z Consumers in Mexico City
latest.abstract: To analyze the relationship between attitudes, emotions, and socially responsible identity among Generation Z consumers living in Mexico City, considering the mediating role of emotions in responsible food consumption. The study employed a cross-sectional design with 514 young participants from Generation Z. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on previously validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to analyze the data. The findings revealed that favorable attitudes toward socially responsible food consumption were significantly associated with emotions and with the development of a socially responsible identity. In addition, emotions statistically mediated the association between attitudes and identity. The results underscore the importance of understanding the role of emotional factors in consumer decision-making within the framework of socially responsible identity among Generation Z consumers. The study presents limitations related to its cross-sectional design and the geographic scope of the sample, which was limited to participants from Mexico City. These findings underscore the importance of furthering the debate on the relationships among the study variables in other Mexican contexts and emerging economies.

latest.title: Looking into the Gap: The Mediating Role of Perceived Control and Intrinsic Norms Between Concern for the Future and Responsible Consumption Intentions
latest.abstract: In the pursuit of socially and environmentally conscious consumer behavior, the core challenge lies not just in identifying motivations, but in explaining how core values, intrinsic norms, and attitudes translate into actual intentions. This dynamic is particularly pronounced in Latin America, where socioeconomic constraints and weak regulations on responsible products actively challenge a consumer’s sense of moral obligation and perceived behavioral control. To decode this complexity, this paper applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to a sample of 643 consumers in Argentina, examining how environmental and social concerns intersect with intrinsic norms and perceived control to shape responsible purchasing intentions. Empirical findings reveal that environmental and social concerns do not directly drive purchasing intentions, rather, their influence operates through a competitive mediation pattern powered by intrinsic norms and perceived control. This demonstrates that concerns remain latent unless activated by personal agency and internalized moral obligations to guide sustainable choices. This research bridges the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theory, offering vital theoretical insights into how altruistic values, moral norms, and cognitive control efforts intersect in consumer decision-making. By highlighting these critical mediating pathways, this study provides a deeper look into consumer psychology, capturing the sophisticated sensemaking and adaptive agency consumers deploy when navigating adverse market conditions.

latest.title: Examining the Effect of Influencer Credibility and Social Media Exposure on Consumer Buying Behaviour: The Mediating role of Consumer Trust towards Cosmetic Products
latest.venue: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications archive
latest.abstract: The expansion of social media has transformed the way consumers acquire product information and make purchasing decisions. The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of Influencer credibility and Social media exposure on Consumer buying behaviour, with mediating role of Consumer trust towards Cosmetic products. Primary data were obtained through a structured online questionnaire from 350 consumers in Chennai city, India, who had prior experience in purchasing cosmetic products online. A Purposive sampling technique was employed to select respondents based on predefined eligibility criteria. The obtained data were analysed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess the measurement and structural models and test the proposed relationships among the study constructs. The result reveal that influencer credibility shows significant positive effect on Consumer trust (β = 0.871, p

latest.title: Speaking to the Heart or the Mind? A Dual‐Process Model of Bilingual Prosocial Behavior in Human and GPT Synthetic Participants
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This research examines how the language of a charitable appeal influences bilingual consumers' prosocial intention and behavior. Drawing on the dual‐process model of sympathy and deliberation, we propose that native‐ and nonnative‐language appeals jointly activate emotive and cognitive routes to prosocial behavior. Two human experiments and two GPT‐based simulations test this account among Mandarin‐English bilingual consumers. Results show that Mandarin appeals elicited stronger sympathy and prosocial behavior through an affective route (Mandarin → ↑ sympathy → ↑ prosocial behavior), whereas English appeals operated through a cognitive route in which perceived self‐other overlap offsets an otherwise lower level of sympathy, increasing prosocial behavior (English → ↑ self‐other overlap → ↑ sympathy → ↑ prosocial behavior). Two GPT simulations reproduced the direction of every mediation path. The findings contribute to bilingual persuasion research by showing that language choice is not just a matter of translation but a strategic lever that influences which psychological pathway an appeal activates. For marketers and nonprofits in linguistically diverse markets, our findings offer a practical framework for aligning language choice with the pathway most likely to drive donor response. The dual‐process model may also extend to other persuasion contexts, such as health, sustainability, and public policy communication, where the choice between a native and a nonnative language can similarly determine whether an affective or cognitive pathway is activated.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: Impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior: role of credibility, perceived authenticity, and sustainability
hot.abstract: Introduction Social media advertising is a crucial factor for predicting consumer behavior. Further credibility, authenticity, and sustainability of social postings enhance consumer purchase intentions in general and online shopping in particular. This empirical study investigated the impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior and the role of credibility, perceived authenticity and sustainability. The study also investigated the mediating effect of trust in the relationship between social media advertising and consumer behavior. Methods To measure the impact of the social media advertising effect on consumer behavior, eight reflective constructs, namely, credibility, sustainability, perceived authenticity, social media advertising effectiveness, satisfaction, purchase intentions and perceived value, were assessed. For the mediation analysis, consumer behavior was modeled as a higher-order construct with three sub-dimensions: satisfaction, perceived value and purchase intentions. Furthermore, the construct social media effectiveness is also modeled as a higher-order construct with four sub-dimensions: credibility, sustainability, authenticity and social media advertisement effectiveness. The data were collected from active social media users who engage in brand advertising and online shopping. A total of 500 valid responses were subjected to exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling. Results and discussion The SEM results reveal that constructs credibility and sustainability are strong predictors of consumer behavior in the context of social media advertising effectiveness. The mediating variable of trust partially mediated the relationship between social media effectiveness and consumer beh

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Recommendations and Functional Food Purchases: Understanding Consumer Decision-Making
hot.abstract: Amid rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), personalized recommendation systems have become a key factor shaping consumer decision-making in functional food purchases. However, the influence of AI recommendation characteristics on purchase intention, particularly the underlying mediating mechanisms, remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how AI recommendation features (personalization and transparency), along with functional food attributes (perceived health benefits and perceived naturalness), influence purchase intention through the mediating roles of perceived packaging and perceived value. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, data were collected via a structured questionnaire survey, and structural equation modeling was employed for hypothesis testing and model validation. The results indicate that AI recommendation personalization significantly enhances purchase intention both directly and indirectly, while transparency influences purchase intention only through perceived value, emphasizing its role in fostering trust rather than directly driving purchasing behavior. Additionally, perceived health benefits positively influence purchase intention both directly and through mediation, whereas perceived naturalness affects purchase intention only indirectly via perceived value. These findings contribute to consumer behavior research by elucidating psychological mechanisms underlying AI-driven purchase decisions while also providing insights for functional food marketers on how to effectively integrate AI recommendation systems to enhance consumer engagement.

hot.title: The Evolution of Digital Tourism Marketing: From Hashtags to AI-Immersive Journeys in the Metaverse Era
hot.abstract: This study examines how social media platforms influence tourism marketing strategies, consumer perceptions, and travel behaviors, addressing their sustainability implications. It aims to evaluate the current state of research on social media in tourism marketing, identify dominant trends, assess empirical evidence of impact, and critically highlight research gaps. The analysis focuses on three core marketing outcomes: destination image, travel intention, and user engagement—and includes a section examining sustainability considerations across environmental, sociocultural, and economic dimensions. The study uses a systematic critical review of 147 peer-reviewed academic articles published between 2015 and 2025, combined with a meta-analysis of 38 quantitative studies that report statistical effect sizes. The meta-analysis uses a random-effects model to compare the influence of different platforms and study contexts. Moderator variables include geographic region, platform type, and methodological design. Findings show that social media marketing has a statistically significant positive effect on destination image (Cohen’s d = 0.61), travel intention (d = 0.54), and user engagement (d = 0.43). The analysis also reveals geographic bias, limited research on emerging platforms, and a lack of longitudinal and ethical inquiry. Findings suggest that tourism researchers and marketers may have to adopt more context-sensitive, interdisciplinary, and ethical approaches. Critical sustainability concerns emerge, including “overtourism”, cultural commodification, digital inequities, and algorithmic biases.
