hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Influencers’ Credibility Effect on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Intention
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: In the evolving world of influencer marketing, Artificial Intelligence (AI) influencers are creating significant impact and transforming the approach to brand promotions on social media platforms. In recent times, many popular brands have partnered with AI influencers to engage with their social media audiences. AI influencers have become popular as a novel method for brands to increase customer engagement and create purchase intention, but there is a scarcity of research on this emerging trend of marketing. The AI-based virtual influencers effect on consumer engagement and purchase intention remain largely unexplored. This study used a questionnaire-based survey method and 414 responses were collected. The result from the research shows that credibility, informative value and human-likeness are the major factors influencing consumer engagement purchase intention towards brands promoted through AI-based virtual influencers. The attractiveness and entertainment value of AI influencer’s social media posts affect consumer engagement but exhibit no effect on purchase intention. Theoretical and managerial recommendations related to AI influencers’ marketing are presented.

hot.title: The economics of ESG disclosure regulation
hot.abstract: Abstract We provide an economics-based review of the pros and cons of ESG disclosures, emphasizing environmental disclosures from an investor-centric perspective. Our survey intends to guide corporate management and regulators in navigating the ESG disclosure terrain. Rather than summarizing the vast and growing ESG literature, we assess the economic arguments for ESG disclosure regulation and the form of this disclosure. We discuss investors’ demand for ESG information and its supply by publicly traded firms. We analyze the case for and against mandatory ESG disclosure. Finally, we weigh the efficiency of disclosure requirement characteristics, assuming mandatory ESG disclosure is warranted. We intend to be positive rather than prescriptive, providing a line of reasoning readers can employ to reach their own conclusions about what we ought to do.

hot.title: Unveiling the future of responsible, sustainable, and ethical consumption: a bibliometric study on Gen Z and young consumers
hot.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
hot.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the key research themes and their evolutionary trajectory within the Gen Z and young consumers (GZYC) field, focusing on the interconnected dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. By using thematic maps and co-occurrence networks, the research seeks to identify significant trends and interconnections that shape sustainable behavior among this demographic. Design/methodology/approach This study used a bibliometric analysis of 546 papers sourced from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, following the framework established by Zupic and Cater (2015), Donthu (2024), Donthu et al. (2021) and Lim et al. (2024). Using R and Biblioshiny, the authors conducted performance analysis and science mapping to examine scientific output and conceptual themes within the GZYC field. Findings The performance analysis reveals an annual growth rate of 22.02% in publications, highlighting the increasing research interest in this area. The keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed eight distinct research clusters within the GZYC field, each representing key dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. These clusters encompass themes such as corporate social responsibility, gender and generational differences, green products, food sustainability, pro-environmental behaviors, the sharing economy and collaborative consumption, among others. The thematic maps and evolution revealed that over time, the focus has shifted. The first decade centered on sustainability and young consumers, while the second decade broadened to corporate social responsibility, green advertising and the sharing economy. By 2024, the focus has shifted toward more systemic and psychological perspectives, emphasizing the circular economy, susta

hot.title: How do omnichannel customer experiences affect customer engagement? Theory and empirical validation
hot.abstract: To clarify the effect of the omnichannel customer experience (OCX) on customer engagement , this article empirically analyzes how OCX affects direct and indirect customer engagement intentions. Using data from two surveys (Study 1n = 312; Study 2n = 822) of U.S. omnichannel retail customers, the empirical findings demonstrate that the positive relationship between OCX and a measure of direct customer engagement (i.e., repurchase intentions) depends on the stage of the customer–retailer relationship. Customers’ novelty-seeking and time-consciousness traits strengthen the positive relationship of OCX with indirect measures of customer engagement (i.e., influence, feedback, and referral intentions). The findings caution against oversimplistic assumptions about how customer experiences create value in omnichannel retailing. To boost customers’ repurchase intentions, omnichannel retailers should employ different OCX strategies in different relationship stages. In addition, they can benefit from targeting customers who exhibit high inherent novelty seeking and time consciousness.

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Roles of logistics service quality in shaping generation Z customers’ repurchase intention and electronic word of mouth in E-commerce industry
hot.abstract: As e-commerce continues to reshape retail landscapes, logistics service quality (LSQ) has become a crucial determinant of customer trust, satisfaction, and long-term engagement. This study investigates the impact of logistics service quality (LSQ) dimensions on the behavioral intentions of Generation Z consumers within Vietnam's rapidly expanding e-commerce sector. The research focuses on how various LSQ factors-timeliness, personal contact quality, order accuracy, order condition, order discrepancy handling, and return convenience-affect trust and satisfaction, which subsequently influence repurchase intention and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM). A quantitative approach was employed, gathering data from 495 Generation Z consumers with prior online shopping experience. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the proposed model and its hypotheses. This study found that key LSQ attributes play a significant role in shaping both trust and satisfaction, which, in turn, drive repurchase intention and eWOM. However, the findings indicate that Generation Z's expectations for seamless logistics experiences vary across different service attributes. While factors such as order accuracy, order condition, and order discrepancy handling contribute to satisfaction, they do not necessarily build trust, highlighting the generation's high standards and perception of these aspects as fundamental rather than differentiating features. This study challenges traditional LSQ frameworks by highlighting the evolving expectations of digital-native consumers. It offers practical insights for e-commerce businesses, emphasizing the need for a strategic blend of technological efficiency, personalized interactions, and seamless post-purchase services to enhance c

hot.title: Financially Savvy or Swayed by Biases? The Impact of Financial Literacy on Investment Decisions: A Study on Indian Retail Investors
hot.venue: Journal of risk and financial management
hot.abstract: Financial literacy plays a crucial role in shaping individual investment decisions by influencing susceptibility to behavioural biases such as heuristics, framing effects, cognitive illusions, and herding mentality. While most existing studies have examined financial literacy as a mediating factor, our study is among the first in the literature to analyse the role of behavioural biases as mediating factors in the relationship between financial literacy and investment decisions. Specifically, we investigate key biases, including overconfidence, herding, disposition effect, self-attribution, anchoring, availability, representativeness, and familiarity. Using purposive sampling, we collected 482 responses through a structured Likert scale questionnaire. The dataset underwent rigorous validation and reliability tests to ensure robustness. We employed Python-based statistical analysis and used Pearson’s correlation and mediation analysis to explore the relationships between financial literacy, behavioural biases, and investment decisions. With the help of these methods, we were able to uncover relationships and causal pathways which further our understanding of the role of behavioural biases in determining the impact of financial literacy on investment behaviour. The findings illustrate a notable positive correlation between investment decisions and financial literacy, implying that people with higher financial literacy levels possess greater and more rational financial decision-making capabilities. Other analyses have revealed that biases have a moderating effect on this relationship, showing another path through which financial literacy impacts behaviour at the level of the investor. By placing behavioural biases as mediating constructs, this research broadens the scope of

hot.title: Impact of green advertisement and environmental knowledge on intention of consumers to buy green products
hot.abstract: In recent years, the rising concern for environmental sustainability has reshaped consumer preferences, driving a growing interest in eco-friendly products. Green advertising, which promotes products based on their environmental benefits, has emerged as a powerful tool in influencing consumer intentions and encouraging sustainable choices. Green advertising has transformative impacts on buying intention of consumers towards green products, and this leads to advancement of economic sustainability. This study explorese the impact of green advertising and environmental knowledge on consumers' intentions to purchase eco-friendly products, addressing a critical gap in understanding the psychological factors that drive sustainable consumer behavior. Additionally, the study discusses the role of eco-branding, eco-labelling, and consumer innovativeness as moderators of the intention of green product purchase. The data was collected from 512 Chinese individuals and employed structural equation model for empirical analysis. Our findings reveal that green advertising has a significant positive influence on consumers' intention to buy green products, with environmental knowledge amplifying this effect. Additionally, factors such as eco-branding, eco-labelling, and consumer innovativeness further enhance consumers' inclination towards sustainable purchases. These insights highlight the importance of integrating educational elements into green advertising strategies and suggest that companies should invest in eco-labelling and branding to reinforce consumer trust and engagement with sustainable products. The empirical findings carry implications for refining green advertising strategies, suggesting increased investments in both green production and advertising initiatives.

hot.title: Green export strategies and SMEs export performance: mediating roles of innovation, readiness, and activities
hot.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between institutional support, green export strategies, and export performance among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in various sustainability-focused sectors. Utilising a quantitative approach, structural equation modelling (SEM) is employed to analyse data collected from 227 SMEs in sectors including sustainable agriculture, eco-friendly consumer goods, special woven fabrics, organic food and beverages, green fashion and textiles, and health and wellness. The study reveals a significant association between institutional support and key aspects of green export readiness, green export activities, and green innovation. Moreover, mediating roles of green innovation, green export readiness, and green export activities are identified, elucidating their influence on the relationship between institutional support and green export strategy. Importantly, effective green export strategies positively impact export performance, enhancing SMEs’ competitive positioning in global markets. This research contributes novel insights into SMEs’ engagement in green export, shedding light on the critical role of institutional support and the mediating mechanisms that facilitate the adoption of successful green export strategies. One limitation of this study is the cross-sectional nature of the data, which restricts the ability to establish causal relationships. Future research could explore longitudinal data to further investigate the dynamics between institutional support, green export strategies, and export performance. The findings provide valuable insights for SMEs seeking to enhance their sustainability-driven international business practices. hot.title: Applying the S-O-R model to explore impulsive buying behavior driven by influencers on social commerce websites
hot.abstract: ., videos and articles). When fans encounter these messages, they may make unplanned purchases, resulting in impulse buying behavior, a long-standing issue in marketing research. This study aims to explore the factors that lead to such behavior. Using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model as a framework, the study investigates how interactions between individuals and influencer content (Stimuli) trigger psychological changes in consumers, namely positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment (Organism), which in turn lead to impulse buying behavior (Response). The study surveyed fans who had previously purchased products recommended by influencers, collecting 404 valid responses. The findings reveal that: (1) Consumers' psychological changes (positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment) significantly and positively influence impulse buying behavior. (2) Scarcity, discounted price, review quality, and observational learning also have significant positive effects on impulse buying. (3) Social presence and sense of belonging significantly enhance flow state. (4) Entertainment and informativeness significantly enhance emotional attachment.

hot.title: How perceived sustainability influences consumers’ clothing preferences
hot.abstract: In this study, we explored innovative approaches to sustainable fashion design, focusing on the increasingly prominent issue of sustainability in the global fashion industry. By analyzing consumer feedback in online communities, particularly through a systematic study of user comments on clothing products on the JD.com website, this paper reveals consumers' attitudes, expectations, and suggestions regarding sustainable fashion. The findings provide new directions for improvements in sustainable clothing design. We collected data using Python web scraping technology from the Chinese e-commerce platform JD.com and employed the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) method for text topic modeling. This approach successfully identified three main themes: perceived quality, perceived value, and sensory comfort. Additionally, we employed multivariate analysis of variance to assess consumers' perceptions. Survey data show that consumers demonstrat higher levels of perceived quality, value, purchase intention, and intention to repurchase sustainable clothing compared to traditional apparel. The research findings help apparel companies understand consumer needs regarding sustainability, providing theoretical support for designers and confirming the importance of emphasizing eco-friendly materials and sustainable production in new product development. This research not only provides actionable insights for the fashion industry but also contributes to the ongoing discourse on sustainable design strategies globally.

hot.title: A critical review of the theory of planned behaviour in tourism research
hot.abstract: The Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) has received considerable attention across various academic disciplines and remains one of the most widely applied – yet increasingly critiqued – theoretical frameworks in tourism research. Despite its widespread use, there is a notable lack of critical reflection on its adequacy in capturing the complexity of tourist behaviour and a limited exploration of alternative theoretical pathways. This paper addresses this gap by critically evaluating the appropriateness and limitations of the TPB in tourism research. Special attention is given to the Theory of Reasoned Goal Pursuit (TRGP), a recent extension of the TPB, alongside complementary frameworks from parent disciplines and emerging methodological innovations. The paper concludes that an overreliance on the TPB may constrain theoretical advancement in the field. Future research on tourist decision-making and human behaviour should therefore consider broader, interdisciplinary approaches that more effectively account for emotional, contextual, and cognitive complexities.

hot.title: Circular Economy: Literature Review on the Implementation of the Digital Product Passport (DPP) in the Textile Industry
hot.abstract: The development of a system to store and share key information about productlifecycles offers a key opportunity to improve the textile and apparel industry. Theintroduction of the digital product passport (DPP) serves as an inclusive tool that enablesindustry stakeholders—companies, suppliers, stakeholders, government organizations,public institutions, and consumers—to more accurately track the journey, characteristics,components, and environmental impact of products. This study explores the implementationand potential of the DPP, highlighting its transformative role as a bridge betweentechnological innovation and sustainability in the textile and apparel sector. By providingunprecedented transparency and traceability, the DPP disrupts conventional industryparadigms and facilitates sustainable practices. The findings highlight the DPP’s ability toconsolidate disparate data into a unified system that provides stakeholders with actionableinsights that were previously unavailable. In addition, the study identifies regulatory andoperational gaps and positions the DPP as a pioneering solution to these challenges. This issignificant progress toward operationalizing the principles of the circular economy andfostering innovation along the entire value chain. In line with the European Commission’s2020 Circular Economy Action Plan, the DPP complements initiatives such as the Ecodesignfor Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) and improves product traceability. By providingstakeholders with reliable, comparable data, it supports informed decision making andpromotes transparency, decarbonization, and sustainability. This analysis underlines thepotential of the DPP to transform the sector into a better informed and environmentallyconscious industry.

hot.title: Greenwashing and consumer skepticism toward eco-labels in Croatia: challenges and policy directions
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the roots of consumer skepticism toward eco-labels in Croatia, a market increasingly shaped by greenwashing and regulatory frailty. Grounded in the theory of planned behavior and signaling theory, it analyzes the psychological and communicative mechanisms that underpin trust in sustainability labeling. Design/methodology/approach A survey of 252 Croatian consumers was conducted using regression analysis. Data were collected via the tablet-assisted intercept method in five stores. The questionnaire had 13 Likert items, demographics and one open-ended question. A pilot test preceded fieldwork. In-store context allowed for real-time consumer insight. Findings Four determinants – eco-label visibility, institutional support, credibility of labels and consumer knowledge – emerged as significant predictors of purchase intention. The findings imply that standardized visual placement and transparent messaging are pivotal in reducing skepticism, bolstering trust and fostering environmentally responsible purchasing behavior. Research limitations/implications The study covers one country with a limited sample, mostly younger consumers. It uses a survey, so it does not capture deeper attitudes. Future work should add qualitative methods, include older age groups and compare with other countries in similar transitions. Practical implications Policy suggestions include standardized label placement, better consumer education and digital tools for transparency. Retailers should support eco-labels through loyalty programs and in-store efforts to strengthen trust and encourage sustainable choices. hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als

hot.title: Secondhand fashion consumers exhibit fast fashion behaviors despite sustainability narratives
hot.abstract: The fashion industry contributes 2-8% of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by rising clothing consumption and the proliferation of fast fashion. Fast fashion accelerates environmental harm through rapid production cycles, low costs, and short garment lifespans. Secondhand clothing markets are often promoted as a sustainable alternative, promising extended use and reduced waste. These markets have grown rapidly, with global sales reaching $177 billion in 2022 and projected to double by 2027. Despite this growth, few studies have empirically examined whether secondhand purchasing displaces or merely supplements primary market consumption. This study addresses that gap using a nationally representative survey of 1,009 U.S. consumers. We find that secondhand consumption is positively correlated with new clothing purchases (r = 0.58, p < 0.01), particularly among younger consumers and frequent shoppers. Cluster and principal component analyses reveal that highly engaged secondhand consumers also exhibit high overall consumption and short garment retention. Although many report high sustainability knowledge, such knowledge does not reliably predict sustainable behavior. Drawing on rebound and moral licensing theories, we suggest that secondhand purchases may psychologically or economically justify continued overconsumption. These findings challenge assumptions about resale's environmental benefits and support policy interventions to realign resale practices with sustainability goals.

hot.title: The Impact of Digital Leadership on Performance: Examining the Roles of Big Data Analytical Capabilities, Green Innovation, and AI Change Readiness in Italian SMEs
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT In today's rapidly transforming world, a leader's digital capabilities have become crucial for firms to achieve better performance. This study examines the influence of digital leadership (DL) capabilities on performance (both economic and environmental) with the inclusion of multiple mediators and a moderator. Specifically, three interesting but complex relationships are examined: (1) the mediation of big data analytical capabilities (BDAC) between DL capabilities and green innovation (GI), (2) the indirect effect of GI between BDAC and performance, and (3) the moderating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) change readiness on the relationship between DL capabilities and BDAC. These relationships are tested with time‐lagged data from 221 small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs). Structural equation modeling results demonstrate that BDAC significantly mediates the relationship between DL capabilities and GI. Additionally, GI significantly mediates BDAC's effect on both economic and environmental performance. Finally, AI change readiness significantly strengthens the ties between DL capabilities and BDAC. The findings extend the leadership, AI, big data, and GI literature and highlight how their interplay can be beneficial for achieving better environmental and economic performance in the digital era.

hot.title: Investigating the factors influencing customer loyalty and the mediating effect of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services: empirical evidence from an emerging market
hot.abstract: This study investigates the factors affecting customer loyalty and the mediating role of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services (OFDS) in Bangladesh. An analysis of 300 responses via structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that perceived food and service quality alone did not significantly impact customer loyalty. While these qualities are essential, they must enhance customer satisfaction in order to boost loyalty. Significant relationships exist among perceived price, ease of payment, time efficiency, and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction acting as a crucial mediator. Strategies focusing on pricing, payment convenience, and timely delivery are the most effective for building loyalty. The interplay between perceived quality, pricing, payment, and delivery efficiency enhances the overall customer experience. This study contributes to the literature by applying Attribution Theory and the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM), emphasizing external factors such as pricing, delivery, and payment ease as key loyalty drivers. The findings suggest that OFDS businesses should prioritize reasonable pricing, efficient payment systems, and timely delivery to foster loyalty. Combined with high-quality food and services, these strategies can enhance customer satisfaction, promote business growth, and increase revenue.

hot.title: Green Branding in the Digital Era: The Role of Influencer Credibility and Greenwashing in Shaping Brand Authenticity, Trust and Purchase Intentions
hot.abstract: This study examines digital sustainability signals and the psychological mechanisms (authenticity and trust) that relate to consumers’ sustainable food purchase intentions. While the attitude–behavior gap remains a persistent challenge in sustainability research, our study focuses on upstream factors that may help explain why intentions vary in strength. Drawing on signaling theory, this research develops and tests a framework that combines positive signals (e.g., influencer credibility) and negative signals (e.g., perceived greenwashing) to investigate the impact on green brand authenticity, brand trust, and purchase intention. Data were gathered from a survey of 324 adult social media users who follow influencers with a focus on sustainability and have recent experience buying eco-labeled food products. Using PLS-SEM, results indicate that influencer credibility has a significant and positive effect on perceptions of green brand authenticity, whereas the influence of greenwashing has a significant and negative effect. Authenticity shows a strong prediction of brand trust, and this in turn predicts green purchase intentions with trust mediating the authenticity–intention relationship to some degree. The results indicate authenticity as a key mechanism by which digital signals affect sustainable consumption. The research provides practical insights for food brands seeking to strengthen the psychological conditions that support sustainable consumption intentions.

hot.title: The Impact of 7Ps Green Marketing Mix on Customer Commitment and Willingness to Pay a Premium Price: Evidence from Vietnam
hot.abstract: As consumers prioritize environmental issues and sustainable development, using green elements in marketing strategy has become valuable. This research examines how the 7Ps green marketing mix influences customer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price for green products, focusing on the role of green brand loyalty, association, and perceived quality. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 571 young Vietnamese consumers reveals that different green 7Ps components exert distinct effects on green consumer-based brand equity (CBBE). While prior research largely focuses on green product, price, place and promotion, limited attention has been given to green human factors, process, and physical evidence, which this study addresses. The findings of this study not only confirm the significant influence of green CBBE dimensions on consumer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price but also enriches the green marketing and consumer behavior literature. Moreover, these provide practical strategies for businesses and policymakers in emerging markets to effectively leverage green marketing, strengthen consumer commitment, implement premium pricing strategies, and contribute to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: Measuring Companies’ Environmental and Social Impacts: An analysis of ESG Ratings and SDG Scores
hot.abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings are central to sustainable investing and research but face criticism for inaccurately reflecting corporate sustainability performance. In response, new metrics have emerged that assess companies’ impacts on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This article compares four ESG ratings with two SDG scores, revealing no correlation between them. It then evaluates the alignment between these sustainability ratings and how investors and regulators assess corporate (un)sustainability. The findings show that SDG scores capture how these stakeholders judge companies’ negative and positive impacts on sustainable development, while ESG ratings do not. This implies that SDG scores have high, and ESG ratings low, construct validity for assessing corporate sustainability performance. These results underscore that concepts like ESG, corporate sustainability, and company impact can be used complementarily but not interchangeably. The practical implication is that sustainable investors should prioritize sustainable development impacts next to avoiding ESG risks.

hot.title: Decomposing Brand Loyalty: An Examination of Loyalty Subcomponents, Product Price Range, Consumer Personality, and Willingness to Pay
hot.abstract: Brand loyalty is widely recognized as a key driver of consumer behavior, significantly influencing their willingness to pay more for preferred brands. This study explores the relationship between brand loyalty, its components, willingness to pay, consumer personality traits, and product price range. A tailored online survey involving participants aged 18 to 60 revealed a strong positive correlation between brand loyalty and increased willingness to pay. The findings also underscore the influence of Conscientiousness and Energy on brand loyalty, alongside the moderating effect of product price range. Specifically, habit-based loyalty dominates low-priced, routine purchases, while higher-priced decisions involve deeper cognitive-affective evaluations. These insights offer valuable guidance for enhancing customer satisfaction and optimizing brand profitability.

latest.title: SMART RETAILING IN INTERNET COMMERCE: AN AI-ENABLED CUSTOMER-CENTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: EPH - International Journal of Business & Management Science
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

latest.title: When AI Says No: AI-Driven Service Rejection and Its Impact on Customer Satisfaction
latest.abstract: Service rejection is common in the service sector and a routine part of commercial interactions. As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into service delivery, it is important to understand how AI-driven rejections affect customer satisfaction compared with rejections made by human agents. This research shows that consumers are generally less satisfied when an AI agent, rather than a human agent, rejects their applications. This is because consumers are more likely to assign greater blame to AI agents, perceiving them as having lower decision-making ability. We also examine how explanations shape consumer responses to AI-driven rejections. Our findings indicate that providing a teleological explanation, clarifying why a rejection occurred, effectively mitigates negative reactions compared with providing a mechanistic explanation, which clarifies how the rejection was made, or providing no explanation at all. This research contributes to the ongoing discussions about consumer responses to AI-based decisions, particularly when those decisions deliver unfavorable outcomes.

latest.title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. Findings It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. Practical implications The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and soci

latest.title: ИНСТРУМЕНТЫ ГЕЙМИФИКАЦИИ В СИСТЕМЕ ВЗАИМОДЕЙСТВИЯ БРЕНДА С ПОТРЕБИТЕЛЕМ
latest.abstract: В статье рассматривается трансформация геймификации из разового промо-приёма в системный инструмент коммуникационной стратегии брендов на российском B2C-рынке. Цель исследования – выявить, какие изменения потребительского поведения и рыночной среды обусловили это закрепление. Методологическую основу составили анализ научных публикаций и сравнительный анализ трёх открытых кейсов: «Плюс Сити» («Яндекс»), «Магазин сокровищ» («Пятёрочка») и «Бьюти-тамагочи» («Золотое Яблоко»). Авторы выделяют шесть факторов системного закрепления геймификации: баннерную слепоту и борьбу за внимание; сдвиг спроса от товаров к впечатлениям; гаджетизацию населения; поколенческий сдвиг (взросление поколения Z); доказанную экономическую эффективность игровых механик; тренды 2025–2026 гг. (фиджитал-форматы и интеграция в повседневные цифровые сервисы). Сравнительный анализ кейсов показывает, что при общей логике вовлечения стратегическая роль геймификации различается в зависимости от бизнес-модели компании – от встраивания в экосистему сервисов до ядра программы лояльности. На основе результатов сформулированы практические рекомендации: определять стратегическую роль до выбора механики, связывать игровой прогресс с реальными действиями и ценностью для потребителя, строить эмоциональную привязку через персонажа и сезонность, развивать фиджитал-формат и персонализацию на основе ИИ, сохранять баланс между монетизацией и доверием, оценивать эффективность по измеримым показателям. Отмечены ограничения инструмента – риск ощущения манипуляции при чрезмерной монетизации и необходимость прозрачной политики обработки персональных данных. Сделан вывод о перспективности дальнейших исследований геймификации в контексте фиджитал-форматов, ИИ-персонализации и интеграции в мессенджеры.

latest.title: Digital enablement and employee performance in society 5.0: a dual-path model of motivation and exhaustion
latest.abstract: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Drawing on Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the relationship between Society 5.0 enablement intensity (S5EI) and sustainable human performance through autonomous motivation and emotional exhaustion, considering human-centric governance capability as a moderator. Methods The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data collected from 519 employees working in digitally intensive sectors in India. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. Emotional exhaustion partially offsets this positive effect through competitive mediation. Human-centric governance capability strengthens the relationship between autonomous motivation and sustainable human performance but does not significantly buffer the negative effect of emotional exhaustion. Discussion The findings conceptualize digital enablement as a dual-valence work condition that simultaneously strengthens autonomy-based motivation and increases digital demands, integrating Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Digital Marketing Strategies for Enhancing Sales Conversion in E-Commerce: An Empirical and Analytical Investigation
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of global e-commerce has intensified competition for consumer attention, rendering traditional demographic-segmented and rule-based marketing increasingly ineffective. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative paradigm in digital marketing, enabling firms to process high-velocity behavioral datasets and deliver hyper-personalized customer journeys in real time. While industry adoption of AI marketing tools is widespread, a substantial maturity gap persists between experimental deployment and fully scaled conversion optimization. This paper integrates a multi-stage analytical research design—combining psychometric Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) of consumer survey data ($N = 420$), econometric before-and-after funnel cohort modeling across retail deployments, and regression-based moderation analysis—to quantify how AI-enabled digital marketing drives sales conversion. Specifically, the study examines four core strategic pillars: neural recommendation engines, predictive programmatic acquisition, dynamic pricing optimization, and generative conversational AI. Analytical results demonstrate that Perceived Personalization significantly enhances Customer Experience Quality ($\beta = 0.499, p < 0.001$) and Digital Marketing Effectiveness ($\beta = 0.488, p < 0.001$), which jointly mediate downstream Purchase Intention and actual checkout conversion ($R^2 = 0.412$). Econometric cohort tracking further reveals a 23.4% to 31.0% relative lift in session-to-purchase conversion rates, a 27% reduction in bounce rates, and up to a 50% increase in Average Order Value (AOV) via real-time affinity bundling. However, moderation analysis confirms that perceived algorithmic opacity and privacy intrusion negatively attenuate conversion gains ($\

latest.title: Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
latest.abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalized artifacts, such as the Skin ID Blueprint, as memory cues; and the expansion of brand associations into skin science and healthy lifestyles. However, the study also found that the campaign's contributions to brand awareness could not be directly substantiated by the Top Brand Index data for the facial moisturizer category.

latest.title: Digital rural transformation, financial assets, and rural household wellbeing
latest.abstract: Existing research treats rural digitalization mainly as a transaction-cost shock and pays little attention to a second margin: by improving access to financial services, markets and investment opportunities, digital rural transformation may enable rural households to accumulate financial assets and thereby improve their economic well-being. Using pooled panel data from the 2015, 2017 and 2019 waves of the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), we empirically analyze the impact of digital rural transformation on rural households' consumption structure and the mediating role of financial assets. The findings reveal that digital rural transformation significantly raises rural households' financial asset holdings and the income those assets generate, and that this accumulation accounts for part of the subsequent shift toward development and enjoyment-oriented consumption. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that younger, more educated, married rural households with higher wage income, loans, and those in less developed regions benefit more from digital rural transformation. The central contribution of this study is to establish financial asset accumulation as a rural livelihood mechanism through which digital rural transformation operates, thereby offering a new theoretical perspective for rural consumption research in the digital economy era.

latest.title: AI-DRIVEN HUMAN CAPITAL DEVELOPMENT: EVIDENCE FROM INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES
latest.abstract: The study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) development and human capital development in the context of technological transformation. The research is based on secondary data from ten large international companies representing technology, consulting, industrial, and consumer sectors. Publicly disclosed corporate information is used to identify AI-related human capital practices, including AI and Generative AI training, upskilling and reskilling, continuous learning, career development, and AI-enabled learning. An AI-related Human Capital Development Evidence Index is proposed to systematize the breadth of documented practices. The findings demonstrate that AI adoption is increasingly accompanied by systematic workforce development and continuous learning. The study confirms the importance of AI-related skills development and organizational adaptability for sustainable human capital formation.

latest.title: Symmetry Between User Cognition and Design Expression: Optimizing Sedan Side-Profile Styling Based on Kansei Semantic Mapping
latest.abstract: The side profile of a sedan conveys visual information about body proportions, stance, line rhythm, and brand identity and is a key exterior element that influences consumers’ emotional perception. In automotive styling, however, users’ perceptual impressions are often difficult to translate into designers’ formal expressions, potentially creating differences between the intended Kansei characteristics and users’ perceptions. This study proposes a perception-informed method for optimizing sedan side-profile styling. It addresses the difficulty of quantifying perceptual information and the limited objectivity of design evaluation. First, the 20 best-selling sedan models in the Chinese market were selected to construct a side-profile sample library. Kansei semantics were collected from user reviews, the literature, and interviews. The semantic material was clustered and distilled using the Affinity Diagram method to establish an initial set of Kansei words, from which Semantic Differential adjective pairs were developed. Second, expert-assigned weights for the Kansei evaluation criteria were calculated using Order Relation Analysis, and a Quality Function Deployment relationship matrix was constructed to rank the importance of styling elements. Finally, three design proposals assisted by artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) were generated under the constraints of highly weighted elements and evaluated using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution. The results identified fluid, expansive and sporty as the Kansei descriptors with the highest expert-assigned weights. A short front overhang with a long rear overhang (B3), a fastback roofline (A4), a rising waistline (C1), an inclined and extended C-pillar (E1), and a teardrop-shaped side

latest.title: Pengaruh AI Personalization Dan Content Marketing Terhadap Brand Love Generasi Z Di Tiktok Shop
latest.abstract: Digital transformation in social commerce has reshaped Generation Z’s consumption patterns, particularly through the implementation of artificial intelligence and the use of marketing content. TikTok Shop applies AI-based personalization to deliver recommendations that correspond to users’ preferences while utilizing engaging content to strengthen consumer interest in brands. This study investigates the effect of AI Personalization and Content Marketing on Brand Love among Generation Z users of TikTok Shop. A quantitative research design was adopted using a survey approach. Data were obtained from questionnaires distributed to Generation Z respondents with previous experience using TikTok Shop. The collected data were examined through multiple linear regression to determine the individual and joint effects of the independent variables on Brand Love. The findings indicate that AI Personalization and Content Marketing contribute to the development of Generation Z’s emotional attachment to brands on TikTok Shop. The results emphasize that personalized shopping experiences combined with relevant and appealing content can support stronger emotional connections between consumers and brands.

latest.title: From negative online reviews to management responses: a bibliometric and thematic review of digital complaint-response communication in hotel contexts
latest.abstract: Negative online reviews make service failures publicly visible and shape prospective guests' perceptions of hotels, with management responses forming part of digital complaint-response interactions. Existing research, however, has often examined reviews and management responses separately, although some studies have analysed linked review-response pairs. Following a structured literature search, this review combines bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis to examine this body of research in hotel contexts. Bibliometric mapping was conducted on 336 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus, followed by thematic synthesis of 103 studies retained through the Web of Science screening pathway. The bibliometric analysis showed sustained growth in this research area, alongside recurring keyword patterns and shifts in scholarly influence. Thematic synthesis showed that negative reviews are often examined within broader review-valence studies. Across the reviewed studies, quantitative and computational methods were common, while direct analysis of linguistic or content relationships within linked review-response pairs remained comparatively limited. This review considers hotels' management responses to negative online reviews as a form of public organisational communication. Limited to hotel-related accommodation studies and selected databases, the review suggests opportunities for future research across broader digital platforms and institutional service settings. Systematic Review Registration Identifier INPLASY202650109.

latest.title: Engagement phenotypes for a sample of 102,684 AI mental health chatbot (ash) users and dose-response associations with clinical outcomes
latest.abstract: Conversational AI chatbots are emerging as scalable mental health tools, but little is known about real world engagement or its relationship to clinical outcomes. To characterize engagement phenotypes among users of Ash, a purpose-built AI mental health chatbot, and examine associations with clinical change and working alliance. K-means clustering across eight behavioral features identified engagement phenotypes among 102,684 users. Subsamples completed the PHQ-9 ( n = 298), GAD-7 ( n = 298), and MSPSS (social support; n = 194) at baseline and 3 weeks; 11,437 users completed baseline Working Alliance Inventory (WAI). Five engagement phenotypes emerged: Early Dropouts (52.2%), Power Users (1.6%), Intensive Users (4.1%), Weekly Users (25.3%), and a novel Concentrated User pattern (16.8%); across users, 66.9% had at least one overnight session (9pm-5am). Significant pre-post improvements occurred in depression ( d = -0.51), anxiety ( d = -0.57), and social support ( d = 0.22). An observed dose-response gradient in self-reported depression improvement was replicated in a larger sample using model-predicted PHQ-9 ( n = 23,813), with the largest improvements among high-engagement Power and Intensive Users ( d = -0.57 and -0.50) and the smallest among Early Dropouts ( d = -0.22). Higher working alliance predicted depression improvement and moderated the engagement-social support relationship. Engagement with AI mental health tools is multidimensional, and different clinical outcomes respond to different dimensions of use. Findings caution against treating session counts as a primary engagement metric and offer naturalistic, correlational evidence consistent with clinical benefit of purpose-built conversational AI, pending confirmation in controlled designs.

latest.title: Digitalisation, Eco‐Innovation and SME Internationalisation: A Dynamic Capabilities Perspective
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). Using data obtained from 300 SME owner‐managers operating in the United Kingdom, the findings suggest that digitalisation positively impacts eco‐innovation and consequently the nature of internationalisation activities. In addition, there is a moderating effect of internationalisation experience on the relationship between eco‐innovation and internationalisation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of eco‐innovation, digitalisation and international experience in enabling SMEs to thrive in international markets. Furthermore, the study offers empirical evidence of how SMEs dynamically develop digital resources, and internationalisation is an outcome of building such capabilities. The implications for practice and future research avenues are examined.

latest.title: Perceived Authenticity in GenAI‐Mediated Luxury Services: The Role of Delivery Configuration and Need for Uniqueness (NFU)
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing integration of GenAI into luxury services raises important questions in a domain where exclusivity, authenticity, uniqueness, and human touch are central. Integrating sociotechnical theory with AI‐in‐service and luxury research, this study uses two experiments to examine how human‐only, GenAI‐only, and hybrid luxury service delivery configurations influence customer evaluations. Findings show that hybrid delivery produces the most favorable luxury service outcomes, with perceived authenticity explaining these effects and need for uniqueness (NFU) shaping customer responses across configurations. This research advances understanding of GenAI in luxury services by showing that its value depends on how human and technological capabilities are combined rather than on either mode in isolation. It also contributes to extant knowledge by showing that authenticity is not merely a stable attribute of luxury offerings, but a psychological mechanism affected by how the luxury service is delivered. Finally, it establishes NFU as a motivational boundary condition that explains variation in customer responses to different luxury service delivery configurations and its interplay with perceived authenticity. Practically, this research offers guidance on integrating GenAI in ways that preserve rather than undermine customer evaluations of luxury services.

latest.title: When Pixels Persuade: Virtual Influencer Content Appeals, Credibility, and Generation Z Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: This study investigates how the emotional, rational and authenticity appeals of virtual influencer (VI) content, together with VI credibility, shape Generation Z purchase intention through perceived content value and consumer engagement. An online survey was conducted among Indonesian Generation Z Instagram users who had been exposed to Lil Miquela’s Calvin Klein content, and the proposed model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility are positively associated with perceived content value, whereas authenticity appeal shows no significant relationship. Perceived content value is positively related to consumer engagement, which in turn is positively related to purchase intention. Perceived content value mediates the relationships of rational appeal, emotional appeal and VI credibility with engagement, and engagement mediates the link between perceived content value and purchase intention. The study extends advertising value and source credibility perspectives to non-human endorsers by demonstrating that message characteristics and source evaluations operate jointly in VI marketing. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of informative, emotionally relevant and credible VI content. The cross-sectional, single-influencer and single-brand design limits causal inference and generalisability.

latest.title: Geopolitical Shocks and Nanotechnology Innovation Resilience: Patent Evidence from G7 and BRICS Economies
latest.abstract: Background: Patent databases are large-scale information systems that record codified technological activity and can support data-driven monitoring of innovation resilience under systemic disruption.Objective: This study examines whether major geopolitical and macroeconomic shocks are associated with changes in nanotechnology patent application trajectories across application domains and whether these changes differ between G7 countries and the five original BRICS countries.Methods: The study combines bibliometric identification of application domains with patent data from the PatentInspiration database for the period 2004-2023.The inferential panel includes seven G7 countries and the five original BRICS countries, namely Brazil, India, Russia, China, and South Africa.Deviations around the Global Financial Crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the war in Ukraine are estimated using event-study PPML models and PPML difference-in-differences models.For the aggregate models, statistical inference is based on a CR2 cluster-robust covariance matrix with clustering at the country level and Satterthwaite-adjusted degrees of freedom; country-specific models are reported only as descriptive point estimates without p-values.Results: After correcting for clustering and the small number of clusters, statistically significant negative deviations during the Global Financial Crisis were observed in healthcare in 2009, in agriculture in both years, and in food in both years.In the 2022-2023 period, only the 2022 deviations in cosmetics and agriculture were statistically significant; during the COVID-19 pandemic, no aggregate deviation was statistically significant.No aggregate BRICS-G7 DiD estimate was statistically significant.The country-specific models therefore serve only as a descrip

latest.title: Agent-Based Simulation of Digital Internal Controls and Fraud Mitigation to Support The Survival of Real Estate Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Under Volatile Conditions
latest.venue: SIAR-Global Journal of Management & Business Review
latest.abstract: Real estate fraud is a growing problem for small business owners in Nigeria, and many firms in Yenagoa metropolis, Bayelsa State, still depend on manual checks that fraudsters can easily circumvent. This study used agent-based simulation to examine how digital internal controls reduce fraud and help real estate micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) survive when the market is unstable. A questionnaire was administered to 180 respondents from 60 real estate firms in Yenagoa metropolis, and interviews informed the rules of the simulation. Respondents agreed that digital verification, access control, reconciliation, audit trails and continuous monitoring reduce fraud, and regression analysis showed that digital controls significantly affect fraud mitigation and MSME survival (F = 149.26, p < 0.001). The simulation showed that adaptive digital controls resulted in the lowest fraud incidence and the highest level of business continuity. Digital controls work best when staff duties are separated and the controls adjust to market pressure, so real estate MSMEs in Yenagoa metropolis should move from manual checks to adaptive digital controls.

latest.title: Governance-ready AI in mental health
latest.abstract: Objective Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots increasingly function as an informal, de facto source of mental health support. This paper develops a governance framework for associated harms and specifies requirements for governance-ready design and evaluation.Method We conducted a purposive narrative review across seven databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar; searches through July 2026) using structured search query strings. Empirical evidence was systematically categorised and distinguished from theoretical psychoanalytic constructs. Findings informed a foundational design analysis of Eva, an unvalidated research case architecture informed by lived experience input.Results We distinguish acute Type I harms (single-turn technical failures) from cumulative Type II harms (multi-session relational risks), characterised through digital psychological harm, the uncanny setting, relational hallucination, algorithmic collusion, AI-mediated psychosis, and epistemic exploitation. Governance-by-design responses include the SAFE-AI (i.e., Screening, Alignment, Facilitation, and Evaluation of AI-Enhanced Interventions) protocol, empathy by design, suitability screening, psychodynamic transcript analytics, bounded co-regulation, data sovereignty, and crisis-safe escalation rather than simulated therapy.Conclusions The central proposition of this paper is that generative AI may support mental health care only when bounded by governance-by-design, clinically informed safety mechanisms, and accountable human oversight, and only once these safeguards have been independently validated. Specifically, we identify three sets of conditions for governance-ready GenAI: clinical conditions, including suitability scree

latest.title: PERAN KOMUNIKASI BISNIS DALAM STRATEGI PEMASARAAN GUNA MERAIH PERTUMBUHAN BISNIS JANGKA PANJANG YANG BERKEPANJANGAN
latest.venue: Jurnal Agregasi Aksi Reformasi Government dalam Demokrasi
latest.abstract: This research, which employs a quantitative approach, aims to understand the role of business communication as a marketing strategy to support the sustainable development of e-commerce in Indonesia. The research process involved the collection of secondary data and a literature review. A sample of 5 online stores was selected from a total of 25, based on the size of their consumer base. The findings demonstrate that the use of business communication to support marketing strategies has been successful in enhancing: a) the number of consumers; b) the consumer base; c) sales volume; d) popularity rankings (specifically for Shopee, Tokopedia, TikTok Shop, Blibli, and Lazada); e) online shopping behavior; f) e-commerce development; g) product categories; and h) payment methods. Consequently, it can be concluded that effective business communication—facilitated through digital advertising in online marketing—can foster sustainable business growth within the Indonesian e-commerce sector. Given the limitations of this study, which relied on secondary data, the author recommends conducting further quantitative research.

latest.title: Capabilities Over Stakeholder Pressure: How Sustainable Learning and Green Dynamic Capabilities Drive Corporate Sustainability Performance
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT With the growing emphasis on sustainable development, corporate sustainability performance (CSP) has become an important indicator of organisations' environmental, social and governance commitments. This study examines the effects of sustainable learning capabilities (SLC) and green dynamic capabilities (GDC) on CSP, focusing on the mediating role of GDC in the SLC–CSP relationship and the moderating role of stakeholder pressure (SP). The proposed model was empirically tested using data collected from organisations in Brunei Darussalam and analysed using SmartPLS. The results reveal that both SLC and GDC have significant positive effects on CSP, whereas SLC also positively influences GDC. Furthermore, GDC partially mediates the relationship between SLC and CSP, suggesting that sustainability‐oriented learning contributes to improved sustainability performance both directly and through the development of green dynamic capabilities. However, SP does not significantly moderate the SLC–CSP relationship, indicating that its moderating effect was not supported in the study context. Drawing on the resource‐based view (RBV) and institutional theory, this study advances understanding of how organisational capabilities contribute to CSP. The findings also offer practical implications for managers seeking to integrate sustainability‐oriented learning and green dynamic capabilities into organisational strategies to strengthen long‐term sustainability performance.

latest.title: Omnichannel Marketing Strategies in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Customer Experience Personalisation and Sales Automation
latest.abstract: Purpose: The research objective is to develop an artificial intelligence-driven omnichannel marketing planning model to personalise customer interactions and optimise a company’s sales. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combines systemic, process and economic-mathematical approaches. Customer journeys are mapped through deterministic identity mapping of events using stable identifiers (customer ID, loyalty ID, hashed e-mail, order ID). Eight contact points were selected. The Omnichannel Data Integration Index (ODII) includes six integration components and two error components. Component weights were obtained by the CRITIC method. Comparison of three planning modes on the same budget of USD 100,000: the baseline channel plan (S₀), independent channel optimisation by KPIs (S₁), and joint journey-based optimisation (S₂). Calculations used a control testing array covering a 12-month period, 8 channels, 3 segments and 3 offers. Research Limitation: The applicability of the results is limited by the accuracy of the input forecasts and the quality of customer data. Findings: The transition from autonomous channel estimation to analysis of identified customer routes distinguished between actual losses and cross-channel migration. Unlike the baseline S₀ mode, the artificial intelligence-driven S₂ mode increased the number of conversions by 13.9%, the marginal result by 11.0%, return on advertising spend by 11.9%, and the target function by 15.5%. Compared with the autonomous channel optimisation S1, the target function increased by 7.1%. Practical Implication. Marketing managers can use it to select contacts, personalise interactions, and allocate budgets. Social Implication: The approach supports more inclusive service provision and helps prevent the widening of the digita

latest.title: Building Credible Sustainability Governance: Integrating Sustainability Performance, Sustainability Audits, and Greenwashing Risk
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT As sustainability disclosure requirements expand and regulatory scrutiny intensifies, greenwashing has emerged as a material ethical and governance risk. Drawing on stakeholder, legitimacy, and agency theories, this study develops a governance framework integrating environmental sustainability, social sustainability, sustainability audits, and greenwashing risk indicators. DEMATEL was used to examine expert‐perceived structural interdependencies among the four dimensions, while PIPRECIA derived priority weights for 22 sub‐criteria. The results indicate that sustainability audit independence, occupational health and safety practices, unverifiable sustainability claims, and discrepancies between disclosed information and actual practices received the highest priority weights in the expert‐based assessment. Kendall's W showed varying levels of inter‐expert concordance across dimensions, whereas Leave‐One‐Expert‐Out analysis indicated that the aggregated priority structure remained internally stable when individual experts were excluded. Overall, the findings emphasize substantive performance, independent audit mechanisms, operational transparency, and verifiable disclosures as central to sustainability credibility, supporting a governance‐oriented interpretation of greenwashing as a systemic rather than solely communicative problem.

latest.title: Humanizing AI : Anthropomorphism, Algorithm Aversion, and Platform Loyalty in Indian E-Commerce
latest.abstract: Purpose : The study aimed to understand the relationship between artificial intelligence anthropomorphism, algorithm aversion, and platform loyalty among college students of Navi Mumbai who had used artificial intelligence-powered shopping chatbots. Design/Methodology/Approach : Questionnaire responses were obtained from 229 eligible college students in Navi Mumbai. As part of the assessment of the measurement model, convergent and discriminant validity were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis. The hypotheses were tested by means of regression analysis. Mediation analysis was conducted with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). Findings : Perceived artificial intelligence anthropomorphism was significantly negatively associated with algorithm aversion and positively associated with platform loyalty. Algorithm aversion was negatively associated with platform loyalty, and the findings supported partial statistical mediation of the relationship between perceived artificial intelligence anthropomorphism and platform loyalty. Practical Implications : The findings suggested that e-tailers could consider consumers’ perceptions of the human-like qualities of chatbots when reviewing chatbot experiences. In the current study, perceiving chatbots as having human-like characteristics was associated with lower levels of algorithm aversion and greater platform loyalty; these findings offered useful insights for e-tailers evaluating artificial intelligence shopping chatbot experiences. Originality/Value : The study provided empirical evidence on the mediating role of algorithm aversion in the relationship between perceived artificial intelligence anthropomorphism and platform loyalty among college students in Navi Mumbai with experience using artificial intelligence shopping chatbo

latest.title: Agile Supply Chain and Organizational Performance of Cable Manufacturing Firms in Nairobi City County, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of agile supply chain on organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Specifically, the study aimed to determine the effect of supply chain flexibility and information integration on organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Methodology: The research utilized a descriptive cross-sectional research design. The target population therefore consisted of 264 staff members drawn from the supply chain/logistics, operations, finance, and ICT departments across the 7 cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. The research utilized a stratified random sampling in the selection of 159 respondents determined using Slovin's Formula. The research utilized primary data collected through semi-structured questionnaires. The questionnaires generated both quantitative and qualitative data. Qualitative data was analyzed using thematic analysis, with the findings presented narratively. Quantitative data was analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics with the help of SPSS version 28 statistical software. Descriptive statistics included mean, standard deviation, percentages, and frequency distribution. Inferential analysis was conducted using Pearson correlation coefficient and multivariate linear regression analysis. Findings: The study found that that supply chain flexibility has a positive and significant effect on the organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. The study established that information integration has a positive and significant effect on the organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya.
