latest.title: Gamification in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Engagement and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In the contemporary digital marketplace, consumer attention has become increasingly fragmented due to information overload and constant exposure to competing stimuli. Traditional marketing strategies often fail to sustain meaningful engagement, necessitating innovative approaches that integrate motivational design with experiential value. This paper proposes the Gamified Experiential Marketing Framework (GEMF), a novel conceptual model that unites gamification mechanics with experiential marketing principles to address declining consumer attention and foster sustainable brand loyalty. Drawing upon Self-Determination Theory, Flow Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, GEMF explains how gamification elements such as points, badges, leaderboards, and narratives activate psychological mediators of motivation, experiential value, and emotional engagement. These mediators, moderated by contextual factors including platform characteristics, cultural context, and demographics, lead to enhanced consumer engagement, loyalty, and immersive brand experiences. The paper contributes theoretically by bridging gamification and experiential marketing, offering a holistic framework that positions gamification as a motivational engine within digital marketing. Practically, GEMF provides actionable insights for marketers to design personalized, ethical, and technologically integrated campaigns. Recommendations for future research include longitudinal studies, cross-cultural validation, and exploration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and augmented reality. By situating gamification within experiential marketing, GEMF advances both academic discourse and managerial practice, offering a pathway to reimagine consumer-brand relationships in an era of attention sca

latest.title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
latest.abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence in Social Media Marketing in Bangladesh: Business Practices, Consumer Perceptions and Challenges
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing social media marketing by helping businesses create content, target audiences, improve customer engagement and optimize advertising campaigns. However, its growing use also raises concerns about data privacy, transparency and consumer trust. This qualitative study explores how businesses and marketers in Bangladesh experience AI in social media marketing, which adoption barriers they face and how consumers perceive AI-driven personalized marketing. Using purposive sampling, 45 semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted, of which 30 complete interviews were retained, and ten interviews were analyzed in depth through thematic analysis guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and consumer trust and privacy perspectives. The analysis identified six themes: AI-enabled content creation and operational efficiency; personalized targeting and advertising optimization; analytics, customer insight and trend identification; automated customer engagement; privacy, accuracy and ethical concerns; and human judgement, skills and contextual adoption challenges. Business respondents generally reported conditional trust in AI, whereas consumer respondents reported low trust and a strong preference for transparency, consent and control over their data. Tentative differences between smaller and larger firms are also discussed. The study contributes to understanding AI-driven social media marketing in Bangladesh by placing business and consumer perspectives side by side and by extending TAM with trust and privacy considerations. Its findings may help businesses develop more effective and responsible marketing strategies and support policy attention to transparency, data protection and consumer confidence.

latest.title: Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
latest.abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

latest.title: Broadband sensor-level EEG power dynamics differentiate anticipation, observation, imitation, and execution of hand actions
latest.abstract: To understand how perceived actions translate to neural processes relevant for learning, planning, and adaptation, it is important to study how sensory inputs and intentions are interpreted within the mirror neuron system (MNS) framework. Although execution, observation, and imitation are commonly studied within the MNS framework, prior reports on cortical activity differences—particularly hemispheric lateralization between left- and right-hand actions and the temporal progression of activity across perceptual, cognitive, and motor cortical regions—remain unclear. Here, we analyzed electroencephalography data from 15 right-handed adults as they anticipated, executed, imitated, and observed right- and left-hand squeezes to characterize task-, hand-, and phase-specific temporal, spectral, and spatial patterns of sensor-level EEG oscillatory power, and to evaluate the within-sample reliability of these patterns. We found that low- and high-frequency EEG power differed by task and hand. EEG oscillatory power patterns were predominantly bilateral, whereas contralateral power modulations emerged during anticipation. Differences in the temporal profile of sensor-level EEG activity were consistent with top-down organization during observation (early frontal EEG power modulation) and bottom-up organization during cue-driven execution and imitation (early visuoparietal EEG power modulation). These findings demonstrate that a single within-subject EEG design can resolve task-, hand-, and phase-specific sensor-level dynamics within MNS-related action paradigms with adequate within-sample reliability, establishing an empirical basis for future hypothesis-driven investigations of sensorimotor integration and perception–action mapping.

latest.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical researc

latest.title: Influence of the rural digital economy on rural innovation and entrepreneurship: evidence from counties in China
latest.abstract: The rural digital economy (RDE) has the potential to support innovation and entrepreneurship in rural areas. On the basis of county-level panel data for China, this study systematically examines the effects of the RDE on county-level rural innovation and entrepreneurship (RIE), as well as the underlying mechanism, by employing a two-way fixed effects model, a mediating effect model, a threshold effect model, and a spatial Durbin model. The results of this study reveal that (1) the RDE is positively and significantly associated with RIE at the county level, an association that survives robustness testing and is consistent with the instrumental-variable estimate, although the exclusion restriction of the instrument cannot be tested directly and part of the association is mechanical because the two indices share an indicator; (2) the relation between the RDE and RIE is nonlinear and is better characterized by a threshold than by a quadratic specification; (3) the estimates are consistent with three mechanisms, namely the development of nonagricultural industries (DNI), higher economic density (ED), and the alleviation of financing constraints (FC), which we interpret as evidence on potential channels rather than as identified causal mediation; (4) a heterogeneity analysis suggests that the positive association between the RDE and RIE is stronger in areas that feature lower levels of modern agriculture, relatively weak information infrastructure, and smaller government size; and (5) the estimates indicate positive spatial spillovers from the RDE to RIE, and the estimated spillover across the truncated weight matrices rises to a maximum and then declines, a pattern consistent with attenuation but conditional on the specified weight matrix. This study provides empirical evide

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence dalam Layanan Keuangan Syariah: Rekonstruksi Perlindungan Konsumen Berbasis Maqashid al-Shariah
latest.abstract: Purpose: Artikel ini bertujuan merekonstruksi model perlindungan konsumen pada layanan keuangan syariah berbasis artificial intelligence (AI) dengan menjadikan maqashid al-shariah sebagai kerangka normatif yang melengkapi hukum positif dan tata kelola AI. Design/Methodology: Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan peraturan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan komparatif-fungsional. Bahan hukum utama meliputi UU Perlindungan Konsumen, UU Perlindungan Data Pribadi, UU P2SK, POJK Nomor 22 Tahun 2023, pedoman AI OJK 2023 dan 2025, serta prinsip-prinsip hukum ekonomi syariah. Literatur ilmiah 2022-2026 dianalisis secara tematik. Findings: Temuan menunjukkan bahwa rezim perlindungan konsumen telah memuat prinsip transparansi, perlakuan adil, keamanan data, pengaduan, dan tanggung jawab pelaku usaha, tetapi belum sepenuhnya mengantisipasi keputusan algoritmik yang opak, bias data, personalisasi manipulatif, serta ketidakjelasan pertanggungjawaban manusia. Rekonstruksi yang ditawarkan adalah Maqashid-Based AI Consumer Protection yang memadukan hifz al-mal, hifz al-nafs, hifz al-aql, hifz al-din, dan hifz al-nasl dengan explainability, fairness, human oversight, privacy, sharia review, dan effective remedy. Practical Implications: Model tersebut dapat menjadi acuan bagi bank syariah, fintech syariah, Dewan Pengawas Syariah, dan regulator dalam merancang, mengaudit, dan mengevaluasi sistem AI berisiko tinggi. Originality/Value: Kebaruan artikel terletak pada penggeseran perlindungan konsumen dari pendekatan kepatuhan pasif menuju perlindungan preventif, dapat dijelaskan, dapat diaudit, dan berorientasi kemaslahatan.

latest.title: Fintech, Financial Performance, and Financial Stability: A Hybrid Literature Review
latest.abstract: The relationship between financial technology (FinTech), financial performance, and financial stability has become an increasingly important issue in banking and financial services. This review examines how digital banking, payment technologies, platform finance, artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, and open banking influence profitability, operating efficiency, risk-taking, and resilience. Rather than assuming that technological adoption produces uniformly positive outcomes, the review focuses on the conditions under which FinTech creates financial value and the circumstances in which it introduces new vulnerabilities. The paper follows a hybrid review structure that combines a systematic search protocol with bibliographic mapping logic and qualitative content analysis. The literature is organised into three thematic clusters: (1) FinTech, bank performance, and competitive dynamics; (2) FinTech, bank risk-taking, and financial stability; and (3) digital innovation, financial inclusion, and the transformation of financial intermediation. Three cluster-based review tables summarise the research streams, representative studies, analytical approaches, theoretical foundations, and reported outcomes. The synthesis indicates that FinTech can improve efficiency, customer reach, innovation, and selected dimensions of bank stability. However, results are contingent on institutional context, bank characteristics, governance, technology integration, and regulatory capacity. Competition may compress incumbent margins, while cyber exposure, model risk, third-party concentration, and rapid digital funding movements can weaken resilience. The review contributes an integrated framework in which FinTech affects financial performance through efficiency, innovation, and informat

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Purchase Behavior: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends and Emerging Directions
latest.abstract: This study maps the academic research landscape on artificial intelligence (AI) and consumer purchase through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed journal articles from 2020 to 2025. A structured search of titles, abstracts and keywords in Scopus yielded 343 journal articles after excluding conference proceedings, book chapters and other source types. We examined the corpus along five dimensions: document and source types, the evolution of published studies since 2020, the distribution of subject areas, keyword co-occurrence, and citation metrics for highly cited articles. The publication output grew gradually from 2020 to 2023 and increased significantly from 2024 onwards, with 2025 recording the highest number of publications. This growth coincides with the mainstreaming of conversational AI and the advent of generative AI. The field is interdisciplinary, spanning business and management, computer science, the social sciences, psychology and decision sciences. Keyword co-occurrence analysis indicates that purchase intention, consumer behavior, marketing and sales are the conceptual anchors and the most cited articles focus on technology acceptance, trust, chatbot purchase intention, virtual influencer marketing and environmental sustainability. This study provides a quantitative map of the literature on AI and consumer purchase for 2020-2025 and highlights the dominant role of trust and perceived value in the literature, as well as open questions about long-term effects and cross-cultural generalizability.

latest.title: Measuring Consumer Cultural Intelligence and Customer Satisfaction through AI Chatbot Service with the Mediating Role of Communication: Evidence from Shopee Users in Malaysia
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between four dimensions of CQ (metacognitive, cognitive, motivational, and behavioral) and satisfaction with the communication of Shopee's AI chatbots, as well as whether such relationships are statistically explained by the perception of the quality of communication. CQ in a multi-ethnic market, like Malaysia, in customers' encounters with chatbots has been under-researched. The subjects were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling to yield 196 valid responses from Malaysian consumers aged 18 to 24 who used Shopee's chatbot or in-app virtual customer service in the last six months and were sampled quantitatively in a cross-sectional design. There were 35 items on a Likert scale, which measured six constructs, and the data were analyzed using reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Sobel tests in SPSS. All constructs were reliable (? = .803–.852). The four CQ dimensions accounted for 58.0% of the variance in satisfaction, with motivational (? = .383), metacognitive (? = .357), behavioral (? = .162), and cognitive (? = .130) CQ having the largest standardized beta coefficients. The quality of communication was strongly correlated with satisfaction (r = .714), and Sobel tests were significant for all four dimensions of CQ (all between Z = 5.71 and 6.31, p < .001), with bootstrap confidence intervals excluding zero and direct effects remaining significant (partial mediation). The construct with the lowest score (M = 2.96) was Satisfaction (M = 2.96), while CQ means ranged between 3.68 and 4.22. The results bring CQ to human-AI service interactions and call for platforms to design for CQ. Since this information is cross-sectional and self-reported, these findings suggest associations, not causal re

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence Disclosure as an Emerging Dimension of Corporate Social Responsibility: Evidence From the Euronext 100
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into corporate business models has led to an ever‐increasing demand for transparency regarding how organisations communicate their adoption, governance and responsible use of these technologies. Despite the rapid expansion of AI in the corporate environment, empirical evidence on the factors determining its disclosure remains limited. This study analyses the factors influencing the disclosure of AI‐related information among companies in the Euronext 100 index, examining AI transparency as an emerging area of corporate transparency with potential implications for corporate social responsibility and non‐financial reporting. Drawing on Legitimacy Theory, Agency Theory and Signalling Theory, the research examines whether firm size, financial profitability and indebtedness explain differences in disclosure practices. Using multivariate regression models applied to 100 large listed European companies, the final models yield an adjusted R 2 ranging from 0.058 to 0.111. The results show that firm size is positively associated with AI disclosure and is the factor with the most consistent evidence, although its statistical significance depends on the specification used. Financial profitability shows a significant association in only one of the selected models, whilst debt does not show a robust association. These findings suggest that the disclosure of information on AI could be related to factors of corporate visibility and legitimacy pressures, although the limited explanatory power of the models means the results should be interpreted with caution. The study contributes to the literature on sustainability and corporate social responsibility by extending the analysis of non‐financial reporting to the emerging fiel

latest.title: Business Intelligence and Analytics in U.S. Financial Services: Evidence on Lending Decisions, Risk, and Governance
latest.venue: Cureus Journal of Business and Economics.
latest.abstract: Banks, FinTech lenders, and other U.S. financial-service firms increasingly use analytics to screen borrowers, verify information, price risk, allocate credit, monitor conduct, and support operational decisions. This structured narrative review synthesizes 47 U.S. empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2026. The evidence is concentrated in mortgage, consumer, small-business, marketplace, and related lending, with additional studies of bank information technology, information-sharing systems, automated underwriting, application programming interfaces, regulatory technology, robo-advice, and artificial intelligence-related operational risk. Several studies associated digital verification, alternative data, and stronger information-processing capability with faster processing, wider credit access, better screening, or improved loan performance. Others reported higher default, mispriced risk, suspicious lending patterns, persistent pricing disparities, and operational losses. Findings varied by setting and research design. Across the settings represented in the evidence base, analytics contributed most to decision quality when information was credible and decision-relevant, useful complementary information was retained, analytical signals influenced institutional action, and incentives, governance, risk controls, and monitoring supported appropriate use.

latest.title: Controlling Differently: Internal Control Digitalization as a Dynamic Capability. A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions
latest.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
latest.abstract: The digitalization of internal control is widely presented as a lever of performance, yet the mechanisms behind this contribution remain unclear. This article argues that the dominant readings of the phenomenon, whether technical, compliance-based, or resource-based, share a common assumption: they treat digitalization as a state rather than as an ability, which prevents them from explaining why comparable tools produce different outcomes and why well-performing control systems become obsolete. Drawing on an integrative literature review and a theory adaptation approach, the article reinterprets internal control digitalization through dynamic capabilities theory. It distinguishes technological resources, operational capabilities, and dynamic capabilities, and defines internal control digitalization as a capability combining continuous risk sensing, deliberate response, and ongoing reconfiguration of the control system. This reinterpretation uncovers a tension between reconfiguration and the stability on which control reliability rests, and introduces the concept of reconfiguration governance, which is distinguished from IT change management and structured around five dimensions. Six propositions follow. The capability affects organizational performance mainly through two parallel and partial mediators, risk management effectiveness and internal control reliability, provided that data are of adequate quality and that automated controls remain under human oversight. Reconfiguration governance determines whether the capability strengthens or weakens control reliability, environmental dynamism moderates the relationship in an inverted U-shaped manner, and institutional pressures weaken it only when they lead to symbolic adoption. The article confronts these propositions wit

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
