latest.title: Digital enablement and employee performance in society 5.0: a dual-path model of motivation and exhaustion
latest.abstract: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Drawing on Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the relationship between Society 5.0 enablement intensity (S5EI) and sustainable human performance through autonomous motivation and emotional exhaustion, considering human-centric governance capability as a moderator. Methods The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data collected from 519 employees working in digitally intensive sectors in India. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. Emotional exhaustion partially offsets this positive effect through competitive mediation. Human-centric governance capability strengthens the relationship between autonomous motivation and sustainable human performance but does not significantly buffer the negative effect of emotional exhaustion. Discussion The findings conceptualize digital enablement as a dual-valence work condition that simultaneously strengthens autonomy-based motivation and increases digital demands, integrating Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.

latest.title: Earnings Management in De-SPAC Companies
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
latest.abstract: This research examines the earnings management practices of companies that complete a merger with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) compared with companies that go public through traditional initial public offerings (IPOs). Using a sample of U.S. firms that went public via de-SPAC transactions and traditional IPOs from 2019 to 2023, we find that de-SPAC companies engage in higher levels of accruals management but show no significant difference in real earnings management. This study contributes to the understanding of the financial reporting practices of de-SPAC companies and their implications for investors and regulators.

latest.title: Business Growth and Development in Pakistan: The Role of Entrepreneurship, Diversification, and Long-Term Planning
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Business growth is an important part of economic development. It supports employment, encourages innovation, strengthens industries, and creates opportunities for individuals and communities. In Pakistan, businesses of different sizes contribute to economic activity through investment, trade, services, and enterprise development. Understanding business growth and development in Pakistan requires examining how companies adapt to changing markets, diversify their operations, develop professional capabilities, and build sustainable business models. As the country's business environment continues to evolve, entrepreneurship, strategic planning, and responsible investment remain important factors in building successful enterprises. Understanding Business Growth and Development Business growth refers to the expansion of an organization's activities, market presence, revenue, workforce, or operational capacity. Business development is a broader process that involves identifying opportunities, establishing partnerships, improving services, and creating strategies for long-term progress. In Pakistan, businesses operate across sectors such as real estate, agriculture, manufacturing, technology, retail, tourism, and hospitality. Each sector presents different opportunities and challenges, making adaptability and informed decision-making essential for sustainable growth. Companies that understand market demand and invest in their operational capabilities are better positioned to respond to changing customer expectations and economic conditions. The Role of Entrepreneurship in Pakistan's Economy Entrepreneurship contributes to economic development by introducing new products, services, and business ideas. Startups and small businesses can address local market needs, create employmen

latest.title: Green influencers and social media environmental advocacy in shaping sustainable fashion consumption behavior among Ethiopian Generation Z consumers
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Generation Z consumers represent the most environmentally conscious demographic cohort globally, yet they are also the most exposed to social media marketing and influencer content. In Ethiopia, where Gen Z comprises over 40% of the population and the fashion market is rapidly developing, understanding how green influencers and social media environmental advocacy relate to sustainable fashion consumption behavior is critically important. This study examines these relationships with a specific focus on the mediating role of environmental attitude and the moderating role of environmental self-identity within an integrated theoretical framework combining Social Learning Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior. Methods A cross-sectional explanatory design with a quantitative approach was employed. Data were collected from 512 Ethiopian Gen Z consumers (aged 18–28 years) across four major cities (Addis Ababa, Bahir Dar, Hawassa, and Adama) using a structured questionnaire focused on sustainable fashion consumption. Multi-stage stratified random sampling ensured representativeness across geographic, age, and gender strata. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0, incorporating bootstrapping with 5000 subsamples for mediation and moderation testing. Results Green influencer credibility demonstrated a significant positive association with environmental attitude (β = 0.216, t = 3.587, p < 0.001). Social media environmental advocacy showed a significant positive association with environmental attitude (β = 0.221, t = 4.977, p < 0.001). Environmental attitude was strongly associated with sustainable fashion consumption behavior (β = 0.306, t = 7.382, p < 0.001). The model explained 10.3% of the v

latest.title: Pengaruh Citra Merek Dan Electronic Word of Mouth (E-WOM) Terhadap Minat Beli Eyeshadow Pinkflash Pada Mahasiswi UNPI Cianjur
latest.abstract: Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mempelajari bagaimana citra merek dan electronic word of mouth (E-WOM) mempengaruhi keinginan mahasiswi Universitas Putra Indonesia Cianjur untuk membeli eyeshadow Pinkflash. Studi ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif, dan jenis penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif dan asosiatif. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner. Sampelnya terdiri dari 65 orang yang dipilih secara acak dengan metode Probability Sampling. Uji validitas, reliabilitas, asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, koefisien determinasi, uji t, uji F digunakan untuk menganalisis data menggunakan SPSS 31. Penelitian menunjukkan bahwa citra merek mempengaruhi minat beli secara positif dan signifikan, dengan nilai t hitung 2,406 dan signifikansi 0,019. E-WOM memiliki pengaruh yang positif dan signifikan, dengan nilai t hitung sebesar 2,204 dan nilai signifikansi 0,031. Secara bersamaan, Citra Merek dan E-WOM mempengaruhi Minat Beli secara positif dan signifikan dengan nilai F hitung sebesar 100,780 dan tingkat signifikansi 0,001. Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,757 menunjukkan bahwa kedua variabel menjelaskan 75,7% variasi Minat Beli. Disarankan perusahaan memperkuat citra merek, meningkatkan kualitas produk dan komunikasi digital, serta mendorong ulasan konsumen yang jujur dan berisi informasi.

latest.title: The Influence of Consumer Ethnocentrism on Willingness to Buy Through Product Judgment in The Local Footwear Industry
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to describe Consumer Ethnocentrism, Product Judgment, and Willingness to Buy, and to examine the influence of Consumer Ethnocentrism on Willingness to Buy through Product Judgment in the local footwear industry. Research Method: This study employs a quantitative approach using descriptive and verificative methods. The population consists of 66,989,000 income-earning Generation Z individuals in Indonesia, with a sample of 349 respondents selected through simple random sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with IBM SPSS AMOS 24. Results and Discussion: The results indicate that Consumer Ethnocentrism, Product Judgment, and Willingness to Buy are all in the good category. The overall model demonstrates a good fit based on the goodness-of-fit indices. Hypothesis testing confirms that Consumer Ethnocentrism has a positive and significant effect on Willingness to Buy through Product Judgment, with a Critical Ratio of 12.764 (>1.96) and a standardized total effect of 0.721. The model explains 53% of the variance in Willingness to Buy. Implications: The findings suggest that local footwear brands should strengthen consumers’ positive product evaluations through product quality improvement, local culture-based storytelling, and word-of-mouth strategies to increase Generation Z’s willingness to buy. Originality: This study contributes by demonstrating the mediating role of Product Judgment in the relationship between Consumer Ethnocentrism and Willingness to Buy in the context of Indonesia’s local footwear industry, particularly among Generation Z consumers.

latest.title: The Role of Digital Marketing In Indonesia’s Energy Transition:Understanding Electric Motorcycle Purchase Decisions Through Influencer Marketing and Product Quality
latest.venue: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)
latest.abstract: Indonesia’s energy transition is increasingly reflected in transport electrification, including the expanding electric-motorcycle market. Yet purchase decisions remain shaped by more than policy incentives and charging infrastructure. This study re-examines three market-facing determinants—digital marketing, influencer marketing, and product quality—and evaluates their relationship with consumers’ purchase decisions. A quantitative survey was administered to 85 consumers who had purchased electric motorcycles. The questionnaire contained indicators for the four constructs and was assessed using validity and reliability tests, followed by multiple linear regression, partial significance tests, and a simultaneous F-test in SPSS. All measurement items exceeded the reported validity threshold (r-table = 0.213), while Cronbach’s alpha values ranged from 0.614 to 0.655, indicating acceptable internal consistency under the criterion used in the study. The reported regression results show that digital marketing and influencer marketing carry negative coefficients, whereas product quality carries a positive coefficient. All three predictors are statistically significant individually, and the overall model is significant (F = 26.959; p < 0.001) with R = 0.703, R² = 0.494, and adjusted R² = 0.475. The findings suggest that product quality is the most straightforward positive lever for strengthening purchase decisions, while digital and influencer activities require strategic recalibration toward relevance, authenticity, and decision-stage usefulness rather than simple exposure. The study thus frames consumer adoption as a market-side dimension of Indonesia’s energy transition.

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Digital Marketing Strategies for Enhancing Sales Conversion in E-Commerce: An Empirical and Analytical Investigation
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of global e-commerce has intensified competition for consumer attention, rendering traditional demographic-segmented and rule-based marketing increasingly ineffective. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative paradigm in digital marketing, enabling firms to process high-velocity behavioral datasets and deliver hyper-personalized customer journeys in real time. While industry adoption of AI marketing tools is widespread, a substantial maturity gap persists between experimental deployment and fully scaled conversion optimization. This paper integrates a multi-stage analytical research design—combining psychometric Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) of consumer survey data ($N = 420$), econometric before-and-after funnel cohort modeling across retail deployments, and regression-based moderation analysis—to quantify how AI-enabled digital marketing drives sales conversion. Specifically, the study examines four core strategic pillars: neural recommendation engines, predictive programmatic acquisition, dynamic pricing optimization, and generative conversational AI. Analytical results demonstrate that Perceived Personalization significantly enhances Customer Experience Quality ($\beta = 0.499, p < 0.001$) and Digital Marketing Effectiveness ($\beta = 0.488, p < 0.001$), which jointly mediate downstream Purchase Intention and actual checkout conversion ($R^2 = 0.412$). Econometric cohort tracking further reveals a 23.4% to 31.0% relative lift in session-to-purchase conversion rates, a 27% reduction in bounce rates, and up to a 50% increase in Average Order Value (AOV) via real-time affinity bundling. However, moderation analysis confirms that perceived algorithmic opacity and privacy intrusion negatively attenuate conversion gains ($\

latest.title: Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
latest.abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalized artifacts, such as the Skin ID Blueprint, as memory cues; and the expansion of brand associations into skin science and healthy lifestyles. However, the study also found that the campaign's contributions to brand awareness could not be directly substantiated by the Top Brand Index data for the facial moisturizer category.

latest.title: Quantitative insights into visitor profiles: Implications for small ski areas
latest.venue: Journal of Outdoor Recreation and Tourism
latest.abstract: Despite the well-recognized economic and socio-cultural significance of winter sports, research focusing on the specific value of small ski areas and their target market remains limited. This study addresses this gap by conducting a quantitative survey of 1089 visitors to small ski areas in the Austrian destination Tyrol. Factor analysis identifies six core value dimensions that drive visitor demand. These dimensions inform a value-based market segmentation, revealing four distinct visitor profiles: emotional-, functional/practical-, activity-, and holistic/family-oriented. The findings contribute to theoretical knowledge on small-scale winter tourism and offer actionable insights for the development of visitor-centered products and destination branding.

latest.title: Generative AI adoption in organizations: A conceptual model of job crafting, employee productivity, creativity and work engagement
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly reshaping organizational work, yet its behavioural consequences for employees remain unevenly understood. Existing research on productivity, creativity and engagement is fragmented and rarely examined within a single theoretical framework. Drawing on Job Demands Resources theory, Conservation of Resources theory and Self Determination Theory, this conceptual paper develops an integrative model of how organizational GenAI adoption affects employee productivity, creativity and work engagement. Job crafting is proposed as the central behavioural mechanism. The model treats GenAI as both a job resource and a job demand. It therefore recognizes a double edged pathway in which technology insecurity and passive over reliance can offset the benefits of adoption. AI literacy, ethical use clarity and organizational readiness are identified as boundary conditions that determine which pathway prevails. Four hypotheses are developed, covering the mediating role of job crafting for productivity and engagement, its moderating role for creativity, and the conditioning effect of AI literacy and ethical guidance. A time lagged, multi source survey design, supplemented by supervisor ratings and an optional field experiment, is proposed for future empirical testing. The paper offers a resource based account of human and AI collaboration. It also provides managerial guidance for organizations that want GenAI adoption to deliver sustainable gains in performance and well being rather than short lived efficiency gains that erode over time.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Effects of Facial Photo Filters on Judgments of Attractiveness and Trustworthiness: An Online Experiment with AI-Generated Faces
latest.venue: Journal of Medical - Clinical Research & Reviews
latest.abstract: Facial photo filters are widely used when sharing selfies, but how others perceive filtered faces has rarely been examined experimentally. In this online experiment, I examined whether a typical facial photo filter from Instagram affects judgments of the attractiveness and trustworthiness of female faces. To rule out familiarity effects, 40 AI-generated (StyleGAN) faces of women (39 analyzed) were presented either unfiltered or modified with a filter that combines soft-focus, contrast, and exposure adjustments. Participants (N = 69, 39 women and 30 men, aged 18–63 years) rated each face on 10-point scales. The four questionnaire versions were randomly allocated to recruitment channels rather than to individual participants, so condition was confounded with viewer gender (filter: 28 men and 6 women, no filter: 33 women and 2 men). Filtered faces received slightly lower mean ratings of attractiveness (Hedges’ g = −0.32, 95% CI [−0.79, 0.15]) and trustworthiness (g = −0.32, 95% CI [−0.79, 0.15]), but neither difference was statistically significant. Mixed-effects models with crossed random effects for participants and faces led to the same conclusion. Adjusting for viewer gender reduced the attractiveness difference to nearly zero but changed the trustworthiness difference only slightly. Gender differences could not be tested. About half of the women and a quarter of the men reported editing photos of themselves. The extent of editing was not significantly correlated with age or education. The findings do not support the assumption that such filters lower these judgments. Adequately powered studies with randomization at the participant level are needed.

latest.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Formation Path of Social Identity and Virtual Community Belonging on Brand Loyalty
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: With the rise of internet technology and social media, virtual communities have become important platforms for communication between brands and consumers, playing an increasingly significant role in shaping brand loyalty. Based on social identity theory and social belonging theory, this paper summarizes consumer psychological cognition and behavioral responses within virtual communities, analyzing how social identity and community belonging influence the formation of brand loyalty. First, it outlines the relationships among social identity, virtual community belonging, and brand loyalty by defining these concepts. Then, drawing on relevant literature and theoretical reasoning, it proposes a theoretical model—"social identity → community belonging → brand loyalty"—to explain how consumers gradually develop brand loyalty through identity recognition, group interaction, and emotional connection within virtual communities. Next, by examining the classification, comparison, and psychologization of social identity, the paper analyzes how individuals identify with brand communities through self-categorization and group affiliation, and further explores how community belonging acts as a mediator in influencing consumer trust, emotional attachment, and willingness to continue participation. The study argues that social identity strengthens consumers' sense of group identity, making them more receptive to the values and culture of brand communities, while virtual community belonging enhances the psychological contract between consumers and brands through emotional bonds and interactive experiences—both contributing positively to the development of brand loyalty. Additionally, the paper discusses the impact of factors such as community atmosphere, interaction frequency, and inform

latest.title: Beyond Mean Differences: A Three-Tier Approach to Level and Structural Heterogeneity in Green HRM Research
latest.venue: American Journal of Economic and Management Business (AJEMB)
latest.abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) research has expanded rapidly; however, empirical studies frequently treat organizations as homogeneous, conflating differences in construct levels with differences in structural relationships. This study addresses this methodological gap by proposing and empirically illustrating a three-tier approach to examining level and structural heterogeneity in GHRM research within a decentralized higher education setting. The research was conducted at Universidade Nacional Timor Lorosa'e (UNTL), Timor-Leste, involving 150 lecturers and administrative staff members equally distributed across ten faculties. Five constructs were examined: Leadership Integrity (LI), Personal Planning (PP), Employee Commitment (EC), Green Strategic Human Resource Management (GSHRM), and Sustainability Performance (SP). Each construct was measured using ten reflective indicators rated on a five-point Likert scale, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The analytical procedure comprised three tiers: descriptive analysis of faculty-level means, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) to assess level heterogeneity, and Chow tests to evaluate the overall equality of structural coefficients across faculties. The results revealed statistically significant differences in construct means across faculties for all five constructs, with GSHRM exhibiting the largest F-statistic (F = 33.984, p < .001). The Chow tests further indicated the rejection of the null hypothesis of complete coefficient equality for the EC, GSHRM, and SP equations, providing evidence of structural heterogeneity. Notably, the largest ANOVA F-statistic indicates greater differentiation in construct levels rather than stronger heterogeneity in the und

latest.title: Omnichannel Strategy towards Impulsive Buying Behaviour through Social Media Advertisements among Generation Z
latest.venue: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications archive
latest.abstract: Social media has evolved into a strategic platform for advertising and promotion, altering consumer relationships with companies as a result of the advancement of information and communication technology. In Indonesia, where social media advertising has taken over as the primary source of information about online purchasing, this study examines the phenomena of greater usage of social media in marketing. The purpose of this study is to investigate how the Omnichannel variable affects impulsive purchasing behavior through social media advertising. The survey concentrated on Generation Z consumers who have purchased Uniqlo merchandise. A questionnaire was used to choose 300 individuals in order to collect data. With the use of SmartPLS software, the data was examined using the partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) approach. The analysis results show that the Omnichannel variable has a significant effect on Impulsive Buying Behaviour and Social Media Advertisement.

latest.title: Digital nostalgia and purchase intention among young consumers: roles of attachment, authenticity and brand trust
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to understand how nostalgia proneness and social media engagement influence consumers’ emotional attachment, perceived authenticity, brand trust and purchase intention in digitally mediated, hyper-connected environments. Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, nostalgia proneness and social media engagement are treated as stimulus factors; emotional attachment and perceived authenticity as organism factors; and brand trust and purchase intention as response factors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted using survey data collected from 501 consumers across multiple sectors in India. Structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed conceptual framework and examine the direct and mediating relationships among the constructs. Findings Results show that nostalgia proneness positively impacts consumers’ emotional attachment and perceived authenticity. Social media engagement positively affects emotional attachment. Emotional attachment and perceived authenticity significantly predict brand trust, which leads to higher purchase intention among consumers. In addition, emotional attachment fully mediates the impact of nostalgia proneness on consumers’ brand trust. The study contributes to emerging digital nostalgia literature by explaining how algorithmically mediated nostalgic experiences influence young consumers’ emotional and behavioral responses, Gen Z and Millennials in particular. Research limitations/implications First, the study used a cross-sectional research design. A causal relationship among the study’s variables cannot be concluded because of its cross-sectional nature. Researchers can use longitudinal studies in the future to understand nostalgic exper

latest.title: From Symbolic Action to Substantive Outcomes: The Positive Relationship Between Ideologically Aligned CEO Activism and Employee Productivity
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue CEO activism has become increasingly prevalent among top executives, yet we know little about whether it is associated with substantive effects on firm effectiveness and the conditions under which such effects arise. Research Findings/Insights Using a panel of 1026 S&P 1500 CEOs observed between 2015 and 2019, we find that CEO activism alignment with employee ideology is positively associated with employee productivity. We further find that this positive relationship is amplified in highly polarized industries and firms. Supplemental mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with our proposed mechanism. Theoretical/Academic Implications The study integrates the stakeholder‐alignment view of CEO activism with the meaning‐making view of executive symbolism to theorize CEO activism as a symbolic action with substantive organizational consequences. Our findings suggest that CEO activism may extend beyond stakeholders' evaluations and attitudes to also relate to the contributions they make to the firm. We also identify ideological polarization as an important contextual condition under which these relationships are stronger, as it makes CEO activism more salient, distinctive, and meaningful to employees. In doing so, we connect CEO activism to a more relational view of stakeholder governance, suggesting that symbolic executive actions may eventually contribute to such governance insofar as they relate to stakeholders' willingness to cooperate with and contribute to the firm. Practitioner/Policy Implications CEOs' public stances on sociopolitical issues can be associated with firm effectiveness when those stances align with employees' prevailing ideological values. Ideologically aligned activism can be associated with more favorable emplo

latest.title: CULTURAL DIVERSITY AND EMPLOYEE RETENTION IN TIER 1 COMMERCIAL BANKS IN NAIROBI COUNTY, KENYA
latest.venue: EPRA International Journal of Economic and Business Review
latest.abstract: Kenya’s banking sector contributes largely to economic development through employment creation and provision of financial services. However, with globalisation and cultural shifts, retaining skilled and experienced employees has become a challenge. Recent evidence indicates that annual employee turnover reported to range between 10% and 15%. Therefore, the general objective of the study was to examine the influence of cultural diversity on employee retention in Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County, Kenya. The study was anchored on the Social Identity/Categorization Theory. A correlational research design was adopted. The target population was 162 employees drawn from the human resource, finance, operations, customer service, marketing, and ICT departments across the nine Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County. Stratified random sampling design was used to sample 115 respondents proportionately distributed across the six departments. Primary data was collected using a structured questionnaire administered through Google Forms. A pilot study was conducted at the Kenya Commercial Bank, Mombasa Branch. The study employed both descriptive and inferential statistics, analysed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS version 21), and data was presented in the form of tables. From the findings, the study concluded that cultural diversity has a statistically significant positive influence on employee retention in Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County, Kenya (β = 0.282, p = 0.000; r = 0.825, p = 0.000). Based on the findings and the conclusions of the study, the researcher recommends that Tier 1 Commercial Banks embrace employees' distinct cultural identities, establish dedicated conflict-resolution mechanisms to manage cultural value clashes, and devel
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Influence of Instagram Social Media, Location and Service Quality on Purchase Interest at Dicendana Coffee Tigaraksa
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Instagram Social Media, Location, and Service Quality on Purchase Intention at Dicendana Coffee Tigaraksa, both partially and simultaneously. The study uses a quantitative method with an associative approach. The study population is consumers of Dicendana Coffee Tigaraksa, with a sample of 117 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics through multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The regression results produce the equation Y = 0.819 + 0.397X1 + 0.191X2 + 0.366X3 + e. Partially, Instagram Social Media has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention with a coefficient of 0.397, t count of 4.120, and significance <0.001. Location does not have a significant effect with a coefficient of 0.191, t count of 1.691, and significance 0.094. Service Quality has a positive and significant effect with a coefficient of 0.366, t count of 3.955, and significance <0.001. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on Purchase Intention with F count of 82.094 and significance <0.001. The R Square value of 0.685 indicates that 68.5% of the variation in Purchase Intention can be explained by these three variables, while 31.5% is explained by other factors outside the model.

latest.title: Through the eyes of an observer: the role of perceived effort in addressing online incivility in social media service recovery
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how firms use different responses to consumer-to-consumer incivility on social media during service recovery. The authors use attribution theory and service climate to examine outcomes of observer perceptions of two response styles, justifying versus denouncing incivility. A key mediator (observers’ perceived effort) and moderator (observers’ consumer-to-consumer justice) are tested. Design/methodology/approach Study 1’s online content analysis illustrates the phenomenon. Study 2 (incivility from a troll) and Study 3 (incivility from a loyal customer) use service failure and complaint scenarios to assess complementary mediation of observers’ perceived effort and service climate. Findings Study 1 finds that firms justify incivility more than denounce it in practice. Studies 2 and 3 reveal that denouncing incivility leads to greater observer purchase and engagement intentions through increased effort perceptions but only if observers perceive incivility as an injustice. Effort’s mediation is robust to controlling another mediator, perceived service climate. Research limitations/implications The authors extend attribution theory with a distinct action and stakeholder conceptually different from a firm’s effort to handle a complainant’s failure. Effort perceptions attributed to a firm are based on an action of handling a nonconsumption failure of consumer-to-consumer incivility (rather than an action of correcting a product or service consumption failure), and this is perceived by observer stakeholders who did not suffer a failure (rather than a complainant stakeholder). Practical implications Firms are eight times more likely to justify incivility than denounce it. However, denouncing unjust incivility from trolls or loyal cu

latest.title: The Role of Social Media Marketing in Client Servicing at Digital Marketing Agencies
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: This paper examines how social media marketing activities support client servicing in a digital marketing agency, drawing on the On-the-Job Training (OJT) completed at Affinity Kraft Solution Pvt. Ltd. from 26 May to 31 August 2026. The study focuses on content-calendar planning, client-specific content strategy, market and competitor research, influencer identification, social media publishing, paid-advertising exposure, performance monitoring and client coordination. A descriptive and exploratory case-study design is used, with a qualitative-dominant approach based on participant observation and review of available work materials. The observations indicate that client servicing is closely connected with the marketing delivery process: understanding requirements informs research and strategy; calendars and creative reviews organise execution; and feedback and performance monitoring guide subsequent planning. The report does not contain a formal client-satisfaction survey or complete numerical campaign exports. Accordingly, the paper presents process-based findings and does not claim statistically measured improvements in engagement, sales, return on advertising spend or client satisfaction. The study highlights the value of customised strategies, structured workflows, relevant influencer selection and clear communication. Keywords—Social media marketing; client servicing; digital marketing agency; content strategy; influencer marketing; campaign monitoring; client communication.

latest.title: Digital entrepreneurship challenge: the effect of website/app hopping on information usefulness
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine website/app hopping as a digital entrepreneurship challenge that shapes consumers' perceptions of information usefulness. Specifically, the study investigates how Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers' digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products relate to website/app hopping and how website/app hopping is associated with information usefulness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a two-study mixed-method design. Study 1 draws on semi-structured interviews with 12 small business entrepreneurs to identify key themes related to Gen Z consumers' website/app hopping. Study 2 tests the resulting model using survey data from 314 US Gen Z consumers aged 18–24, analyzed through exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and multi-group moderation analysis. Findings The results show that pragmatism and preference for curated products positively predict website/app hopping, while digital savviness might serve as an enabling condition rather than a direct motivator. Website/app hopping is positively related to information usefulness. Multi-group analysis shows that for low-frequency shoppers, digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products all predict website/app hopping. For high-frequency shoppers, pragmatism is the only significant predictor. These findings suggest that digital savviness may be an enabling condition, while pragmatism is the primary motivational driver. Originality/value This study contributes to digital entrepreneurship by reframing website/app hopping as an entrepreneurial information-management challenge rather than merely a consumer search behavior. It shows how Gen Z consumers verify information across fragmented digital platf

latest.title: Customer Satisfaction as A Mediator of Community-Based Marketing and Promotion on Repurchase Intention at Fore Coffee Surabaya
latest.venue: Commercium Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of the modern retail coffee industry has created intense market competition, making customer retention a critical strategic priority for business sustainability. This study evaluates the indirect statistical relationships linking Community-Based Marketing (CBM) and Promotional Activities with Repurchase Intention through Customer Satisfaction among FORE Coffee consumers in Surabaya, Indonesia. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, it employs a quantitative cross-sectional explanatory survey design. Primary data were collected from 126 verified FORE Coffee consumers through purposive sampling based on specific eligibility criteria and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). CBM (β = 0.390, p < 0.001) and Promotional Activities (β = 0.411, p < 0.001) show positive, statistically significant direct associations with Customer Satisfaction. Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.509, p < 0.001) and CBM (β = 0.280, p = 0.002) also have significant direct positive relationships with Repurchase Intention, whereas Promotional Activities show no significant direct path (β = 0.090, p = 0.281). Mediation analysis confirms that Customer Satisfaction significantly mediates the indirect relationships of CBM (β = 0.198, p = 0.002) and Promotional Activities (β = 0.209, p = 0.002) with Repurchase Intention. These results highlight that promotional incentives are associated with repurchase intention primarily through the internal evaluative mechanism of customer satisfaction rather than directly driving repeat purchasing decisions. As a result, coffee shop managers should prioritize satisfaction-oriented promotional designs alongside interactive brand community ecosystems to support customer retention within urban ret

latest.title: Premium in English, budget in Tagalog? Modelling the asymmetric meanings of translanguaging for online consumer segmentation in the Philippines
latest.abstract: Purpose Marketing analytics of electronic word of mouth for consumer segmentation treat linguistic markers, such as lexical diversity, code-switching and review length, as universal indicators for consumption preferences. This assumption breaks down in Asia, where multilingual consumers use languages that carry unequal social status. Drawing on theories of indexicality (semiotics) and language as social practice, this study aims to demonstrate that in countries like the Philippines where translanguaging practices dominate, languaging behaves asymmetrically depending on the social status and symbolic capital embedded in the linguistic resources involved. Design/methodology/approach Using large-scale eWOM data from two online platforms operating in the Philippines, this paper conducts three complementary studies using a hybrid machine learning approach. This paper utilizes k-means clustering for customer segmentation and LightGBM to assess the predictive power of translanguaging features. By integrating Explainable AI (XAI) through SHAP value analysis, this paper provides model interpretability by deconstructing how variables, such as English dominance, code-switching, frequency, lexical diversity and review length can serve as asymmetric predictors of purchasing power. Findings The findings demonstrate that the predictive strength of lexical diversity and linguistic purity for premium consumption preferences applies only for English-dominant reviews, with the same linguistic features predicting more price sensitive consumption in Tagalog-dominant reviews. Originality/value By integrating sociolinguistic theory with machine learning-powered marketing analytics, this paper extends eWOM analytics beyond sentiment and brand perception toward a culturally-embedded understandi

latest.title: ETHNIC ELEMENTS IN FILM/ADVERTISING: CONSUMER RESPONSE TO CULTURAL APPROPRIATION
latest.abstract: Ethnic elements, including traditional attire, symbols, music, language, and rituals, increasingly feature in films and advertisements to enhance authenticity, novelty, and emotional appeal. While such incorporation promotes cultural visibility, it often raises concerns of Perceived Cultural Authenticity (PCA) when used without proper context, consent or benefit-sharing, potentially reshaping consumer perception and brand value. The primary objective is to identify consumer attitudes toward cultural appreciation (CA) and assess its economic implications for brands and cultural communities. A quantitative survey was administered to 368 consumers exposed to advertising and film content containing ethnic motifs, complemented by content analysis of 40 advertisements and interviews with 10 marketing professionals. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and regression analysis in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), findings indicated that authenticity (β = 0.34), CR (β = 0.27), and CA (β = 0.21) positively influenced Brand Trust (BT). BT positively predicted PI (β = 0.64). The indirect effect of authenticity on PI through BT was β = 0.22. Qualitative findings reveal brands emphasizing collaboration and accurate representation earn stronger consumer loyalty and economic advantage over competitors relying on stereotypical portrayals. The research concludes ethical engagement with ethnic elements benefits both business and cultural communities.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.
