hot.title: The impact of green HRM practices on green innovative work behaviour: empirical evidence from the hospitality sector of China and Pakistan
hot.abstract: Amid a global shift towards eco-friendly practices, this study investigates the impact of green human resource management (GHRM) practices on green innovative work behavior (GIWB) in the hospitality sector, focusing on emerging and developing countries, specifically China and Pakistan. The research also explores the mediating roles of green perceived organizational support (GPOS) and organizational citizenship behavior towards the environment (OCBE), as well as the moderating role of green transformational leadership (GTL). This study is grounded in the AMO (ability, motivation, and opportunity) theory and organizational support theory. Data were collected through a questionnaire, yielding 503 valid responses from hotel employees in Beijing, China, and 498 valid responses from Islamabad, Pakistan. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to examine and compare the results across both samples. The findings reveal positive and significant relationships between GHRM and GIWB, as well as notable mediation and moderation effects among the specified variables. Interestingly, GTL did not significantly moderate the relationship between GHRM and GIWB in Pakistan's sample, highlighting a regional contrast. This study contributes to advancing the implementation of GHRM practices to enhance GIWB in the hospitality sector, with insights into the role of GTL across different cultural contexts.

hot.title: Gamification for sustainable consumption: A state‐of‐the‐art overview and future agenda
hot.abstract: Abstract Unsustainable consumption is a pressing issue requiring innovative solutions. Gamification is a promising approach with the potential to drive a shift toward sustainable consumption. This study delivers a state‐of‐the‐art overview of gamification as a strategy for sustainable consumption, shedding light on its role at the intersection of environmental sustainability , sustainability education , sustainable behavioral changes , sustainable living , sustainable tourism , and workplace sustainability , underscoring that sustainable consumption (e.g., energy) is not only personal but also professional. This study also offers a rich organizer of antecedents (game mechanics, incentives and mechanisms, social dynamics, sustainability focus, and user experience), mediators and moderators (psychographic and socio‐cultural), controls (demographic and contextual), and outcomes (behavioral changes, consumption patterns, and psychographic shifts), alongside relevant theories and methods , to provide a finer‐grained, toolbox‐like understanding of gamification for sustainable consumption. This study concludes with avenues for future research to drive new frontiers where gamification can contribute to sustainable consumption, and by extension, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12 on Responsible Consumption and Production.

hot.title: Leveraging social media for sustainable fashion: how brand and user-generated content influence Gen Z’s purchase intentions
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines how brand-generated content (BGC) and user-generated content (UGC) on TikTok and Instagram shape Gen Z consumers’ purchase intentions for sustainable fashion. It also investigates the mediating role of social media engagement (SME) in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was employed, using stratified random sampling to target Gen Z consumers aged 16–28. Data were collected from 643 respondents through structured surveys and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. Findings Both BGC and UGC positively influence purchase intentions, with BGC demonstrating a stronger effect due to its professional quality and emotional appeal. SME partially mediates these relationships, amplifying the impact of both content types on purchase behavior. Originality This research advances the sustainable fashion marketing literature by integrating insights from social media influence and consumer behavior, specifically within the Gen Z demographic. Unlike previous studies that focus solely on BGC or UGC in isolation, this study examines their interplay and the crucial mediating role of SME. The findings offer practical guidance for brands on how to strategically balance BGC and UGC to optimize consumer engagement and drive sustainable purchasing decisions.

hot.title: Forty years of the theory of planned behavior: a bibliometric analysis (1985–2024)
hot.abstract: Abstract The goal of the study is a comprehensive and systematic analysis of the literature and research landscape of the TPB between 1985–2024. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric study of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) literature over the past forty years (1985–2024), analyzing 14,461 articles and 542,479 citations published in the Web of Science Core Collection. Utilizing performance analysis and science mapping techniques, the study leverages bibliographic coupling, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and a temporal assessment of the field across six distinct periods (1985–1999; 2000–2004, 2005–2009; 2010–2014; 2015–2019; and 2020–2024). Employing VOS Viewer software for visualization, this research maps the evolution, intellectual structure, and networks of relationships in the TPB field for the first time. The results highlight significant patterns and interdisciplinary connections, identifying the most influential publications, authors, journals, and institutions. A distinguishing feature of the study is the identification of thematic clusters based on multiple criteria and a triangulation analysis of these clusters. Additionally, the study investigates the most influential articles within the six periods and provides an evolutionary phase-wise analysis of TPB. Another highlight is the detailed guidance on future research avenues, which are actionable and based on a rigorous assessment of the most cited articles from 2020 to 2024. The study makes a significant contribution to the ongoing research conversations on the trajectory and growth of TPB across various disciplines.

hot.title: Closing the loop at the local scale: Investigating the drivers of and barriers to the implementation of the circular economy in cities and regions
hot.abstract: Transitioning to a circular economy (CE) at the local level is important for addressing the strain on natural resources caused by population growth and climate change. This study aims to investigate the factors that influence or impede the adoption of CE practices in French cities and regions. To achieve this goal, 47 interviews were conducted with practitioners from local authorities to identify the key elements that facilitate or hinder the implementation of CE. The findings highlight the crucial role of local authorities in enabling the transition to a CE, with critical support from political endorsement, strategic foresight, and effective leadership. However, obstacles such as organizational inertia, financial constraints, and a limited understanding of a CE present challenges to a CE's broader adoption. The study also emphasizes the critical role of partnerships and collaborative networks in overcoming these barriers and promoting the advancement of CE initiatives.

hot.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Factors for Sustainable Tourism Development: The Way Forward Toward Destination Resilience and Growth
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Although environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is increasingly gaining popularity in corporate and financial domains, its application in the tourism industry is still relatively underexplored. Hence, the objectives of this research are fivefold: (1) A systematic review appraises the extant literature on the intersection of the ESG dimensions and sustainable tourism; (2) It provides a synthesis of the content of the extracted articles and maps thematic intersections related to travel destinations' environmental stewardship, social equity and governance frameworks; (3) It assesses ESG‐aligned strategies that are intended to address the destinations' challenges including their carrying capacities and overtourism issues, climate risks, sociocultural tensions as well as institutional accountabilities; (4) It provides a holistic conceptual framework that guides policymakers, practitioners and stakeholders in integrating ESG into tourism planning and development, for sustainable and economically viable outcomes. In conclusion, (5) it advances theoretical and managerial implications.

hot.title: The implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation for sustainability
hot.abstract: The interconnected phenomena of digital transformation and environmental innovation exert a major impact on sustainability . This research attempts to shed light on the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation. Both digital transformation and environmental innovation offer multiple opportunities to address global challenges such as climate change , resource depletion , and social inequality. This study highlights the need to integrate digital technologies and innovation with environmental initiatives. By following this approach, the sustainability implications of digital transformation and environmental innovation can lead to a more resilient and sustainable society. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is used to determine the necessary or sufficient factors to increase sustainability. The study thus provides insights into what the environmental priorities should be. The results show how to reduce environmental impacts , improve quality of life , and support economic development. They can also be used to inform policies that support sustainability initiatives by encouraging the combinations of interventions that work best. By harnessing the potential of digital transformation and environmental innovation, it is possible to build a greener and more prosperous future for generations to come.

hot.title: Toward a Resilient and Sustainable Supply Chain: Operational Responses to Global Disruptions in the Post-COVID-19 Era
hot.abstract: Global supply chains have faced unprecedented disruptions in recent years, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to geopolitical tensions and climate-induced shocks. These events have exposed structural vulnerabilities in operational models overly optimized for efficiency at the expense of resilience and sustainability. This conceptual paper proposes an integrated framework linking resilience enablers, post-pandemic operational strategies, and sustainability outcomes. Through a synthesis of the interdisciplinary literature across operations management, sustainability science, institutional theory, and organizational behavior, we develop typologies of operational responses—including agile, lean–green, circular, and decentralized models—and connect them to broader Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on systems thinking and the Triple Bottom Line framework, we present a conceptual model that outlines causal relationships between resilience drivers, adaptive operational strategies, and long-term sustainable performance. The paper further discusses policy implications for public and private sectors, offering insights for global sustainability governance. We conclude by outlining a research agenda to empirically test and refine the model through multi-method approaches. This study contributes to theory by reconceptualizing sustainable operations in the context of compound global disruptions and offers a normative direction for future scholarship and practice.

hot.title: Exploring moral hazard and adverse selection in the context of greenwashing and organic product consumption
hot.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
hot.abstract: Behavior within the thematic of decoupling and environmental sustainability is critical in understanding the dynamics of greenwashing in retail environments. Decoupling, which aims to separate economic growth from environmental degradation, is particularly relevant in the organic product market, where consumer trust and sustainable purchasing behaviors are essential. This study investigates the impact of greenwashing on moral hazard and adverse selection in the context of organic products in Thailand. Greenwashing, the practice of making misleading claims about the environmental benefits of products, creates significant information asymmetry , complicating consumer decision-making and undermining trust in genuinely sustainable products. Utilizing a theoretical framework based on asymmetric information theory, this research examines how greenwashing influences green skepticism, information asymmetry , and subsequent market behaviors. An empirical analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the hypotheses with a quota sampling survey of 402 consumers in Thailand who engage in varying levels of organic consumption. The findings reveal that perceived greenwashing for organic products significantly increases green skepticism among consumers. This increased skepticism exacerbates information asymmetry, which in turn, leads to both moral hazard and adverse selection in the market for organic products. Specifically, companies may exploit this information gap by exaggerating their products' sustainability credentials, resulting in consumers making suboptimal purchasing decisions. The study provides robust empirical evidence supporting the hypothesized relationships and highlights the need for stricter regulatory frameworks to

hot.title: Digital marketing strategies in expanding the market for MSME creative products in Indonesia—state of art
hot.abstract: Digital marketing strategy is the planning and actions taken by companies or individuals to utilize digital technology to market products or services effectively and efficiently to target markets. In this strategy, companies use various digital channels such as social media, search engines, email marketing, websites, or e-commerce to achieve marketing objectives, including increasing brand awareness, attracting new customers, and boosting sales and customer loyalty. However, challenges in using digital marketing still exist due to the digital literacy gap among creative product practitioners. This study reviews digital marketing for creative products, including social media marketing, search engine marketing, influencer marketing, email marketing, and content marketing. Using Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) method, 22 articles from leading sources such as MDPI, Wiley, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore were analyzed. The objectives of this study are to determine (1) what the definitions of digital marketing strategies and the creative product market are. (2) Which countries have implemented digital marketing in the creative market for SMEs? (3) Who is involved, and how familiar are SMEs with the creative product market? (4) What strategies are used in digital marketing in Indonesia? How is it implemented, what are the challenges, and what is the level of success? (R5): What are the future research and recommendations for digital marketing in expanding the creative market? Future research directions include the application of AI and technology for automated content creation for creative product practitioners, strengthened digital education and literacy, and community-based campaigns that foster collaboration among local creators to build a mutually supportive e

hot.title: Green human resources management and green innovation: a meta-analytic review of strategic human resources levers for environmental sustainability
hot.abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has become a vital lever for driving organizational sustainability, yet the empirical relationship between GHRM and Green Innovation (GI) remains fragmented and inconclusive. This meta-analysis integrates findings from 52 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, encompassing 23,103 observations, to estimate the overall effect of GHRM on GI and to examine the influence of specific HR practices and contextual moderators. Grounded in the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study reveals a significant positive pooled effect, affirming that GHRM is a consistent and influential driver of GI. Among HR practices, green-linked compensation demonstrated the strongest impact, surpassing training and recruitment. Moderator analyses reveal that effect sizes differ meaningfully by industry type, firm size, and year of publication, but not by country development status or statistical method. These results contribute to theoretical advancement by integrating behavioral, strategic, and cognitive perspectives on sustainability-oriented innovation. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers on designing effective GHRM systems that stimulate eco-innovation. This study delivers the first quantitative synthesis clarifying when, where, and how GHRM enhances green innovation across diverse sectors and economies, providing a robust foundation for future research and strategy in sustainability-driven human capital development.

latest.title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. Findings It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. Practical implications The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and soci

latest.title: Designing transparency in AI influencer marketing: a consumer–agency architecture
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to develop an understanding of AI influencer transparency and its effects on affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a conceptual synthesis of influencer marketing, consumer psychology and human–algorithm interaction research. Findings This paper introduces the Consumer–Agency Architecture (CAA) framework, distinguishing between information, control and provenance transparency. CAA posits that effects of transparency on consumer outcomes are driven by reductions in reactance, whether affective or cognitive. Information transparency primarily mitigates affective reactance; control transparency reduces cognitive reactance; and provenance transparency can attenuate both. Lower reactance, in turn, can support the formation of affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. The framework further identifies boundary conditions that either strengthen or weaken the relationship between transparency and reactance. Research limitations/implications This paper proposes a conceptual framework that remains to be empirically tested. It also posits that transparency effects in AI influencer marketing are primarily driven by reactance, not gains in perceived authenticity. The developed model also assumes that transparency forms have distinct rather than additive or even nonlinear effects on cognitive and affective reactance. Such assumptions could be tested in future work. Practical implications Brands and platforms should treat transparency as a portfolio of design levers rather than a single disclosure: match the specific type of transparency to the focal objective, anticipate trade-offs and avoid one-size-fits-all transparency that can erode trust. latest.title: Brand Experience Strategy in Building Wardah's Brand Awareness Through Skinverse Campaign
latest.abstract: Brands with already high levels of brand awareness face challenges that differ from those of emerging brands, particularly in maintaining relevance and memorability amid increasingly intense competition. This study examines Wardah's brand experience strategy through the Skinverse campaign, which was conducted in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and its potential contribution to brand awareness. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design based on document analysis. Data were obtained from company press releases, 17 articles published by national online media outlets, and Top Brand Index data from 2022 to 2026. These sources were analyzed through deductive coding based on Schmitt's five Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). The findings reveal that Skinverse evolved from a science-based educational exhibition in 2024 to an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered skincare clinic in 2025, followed by a skin longevity clinic integrating skin health with lifestyle factors in 2026. Throughout this evolution, the experiential emphasis shifted from the Think module toward the Act module. The document analysis identified four potential mechanisms for strengthening brand awareness: the consistent use of the Skinverse campaign name as a distinctive brand asset; MURI (Indonesian World Records Museum) records and collaborations with experts as drivers of media coverage; personalized artifacts, such as the Skin ID Blueprint, as memory cues; and the expansion of brand associations into skin science and healthy lifestyles. However, the study also found that the campaign's contributions to brand awareness could not be directly substantiated by the Top Brand Index data for the facial moisturizer category.

latest.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Formation Path of Social Identity and Virtual Community Belonging on Brand Loyalty
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: With the rise of internet technology and social media, virtual communities have become important platforms for communication between brands and consumers, playing an increasingly significant role in shaping brand loyalty. Based on social identity theory and social belonging theory, this paper summarizes consumer psychological cognition and behavioral responses within virtual communities, analyzing how social identity and community belonging influence the formation of brand loyalty. First, it outlines the relationships among social identity, virtual community belonging, and brand loyalty by defining these concepts. Then, drawing on relevant literature and theoretical reasoning, it proposes a theoretical model—"social identity → community belonging → brand loyalty"—to explain how consumers gradually develop brand loyalty through identity recognition, group interaction, and emotional connection within virtual communities. Next, by examining the classification, comparison, and psychologization of social identity, the paper analyzes how individuals identify with brand communities through self-categorization and group affiliation, and further explores how community belonging acts as a mediator in influencing consumer trust, emotional attachment, and willingness to continue participation. The study argues that social identity strengthens consumers' sense of group identity, making them more receptive to the values and culture of brand communities, while virtual community belonging enhances the psychological contract between consumers and brands through emotional bonds and interactive experiences—both contributing positively to the development of brand loyalty. Additionally, the paper discusses the impact of factors such as community atmosphere, interaction frequency, and inform

latest.title: Digital nostalgia and purchase intention among young consumers: roles of attachment, authenticity and brand trust
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to understand how nostalgia proneness and social media engagement influence consumers’ emotional attachment, perceived authenticity, brand trust and purchase intention in digitally mediated, hyper-connected environments. Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, nostalgia proneness and social media engagement are treated as stimulus factors; emotional attachment and perceived authenticity as organism factors; and brand trust and purchase intention as response factors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted using survey data collected from 501 consumers across multiple sectors in India. Structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed conceptual framework and examine the direct and mediating relationships among the constructs. Findings Results show that nostalgia proneness positively impacts consumers’ emotional attachment and perceived authenticity. Social media engagement positively affects emotional attachment. Emotional attachment and perceived authenticity significantly predict brand trust, which leads to higher purchase intention among consumers. In addition, emotional attachment fully mediates the impact of nostalgia proneness on consumers’ brand trust. The study contributes to emerging digital nostalgia literature by explaining how algorithmically mediated nostalgic experiences influence young consumers’ emotional and behavioral responses, Gen Z and Millennials in particular. Research limitations/implications First, the study used a cross-sectional research design. A causal relationship among the study’s variables cannot be concluded because of its cross-sectional nature. Researchers can use longitudinal studies in the future to understand nostalgic exper

latest.title: Digital entrepreneurship challenge: the effect of website/app hopping on information usefulness
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine website/app hopping as a digital entrepreneurship challenge that shapes consumers' perceptions of information usefulness. Specifically, the study investigates how Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers' digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products relate to website/app hopping and how website/app hopping is associated with information usefulness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a two-study mixed-method design. Study 1 draws on semi-structured interviews with 12 small business entrepreneurs to identify key themes related to Gen Z consumers' website/app hopping. Study 2 tests the resulting model using survey data from 314 US Gen Z consumers aged 18–24, analyzed through exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and multi-group moderation analysis. Findings The results show that pragmatism and preference for curated products positively predict website/app hopping, while digital savviness might serve as an enabling condition rather than a direct motivator. Website/app hopping is positively related to information usefulness. Multi-group analysis shows that for low-frequency shoppers, digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products all predict website/app hopping. For high-frequency shoppers, pragmatism is the only significant predictor. These findings suggest that digital savviness may be an enabling condition, while pragmatism is the primary motivational driver. Originality/value This study contributes to digital entrepreneurship by reframing website/app hopping as an entrepreneurial information-management challenge rather than merely a consumer search behavior. It shows how Gen Z consumers verify information across fragmented digital platf

latest.title: Between emotion and ethics: a review of advertising appeals, communication and socially responsible consumption (SRC)
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a literature review of the role of advertising appeal and communication on socially responsible consumption (SRC). It synthesizes 75 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus and/or SSCI from the period of 1990–2025. Design/methodology/approach This review adopted a multi-source, iterative search process, incorporating searches via databases, keyword/journal searching, Google Scholar and backward citation searches. Conducted on August 15, 2025, the search provided partial coverage of 2025 publications. Three-stage screening and author-led quality appraisal were applied. The selected articles were analyzed by publication year, geographical context, methodology, respondent characteristics, theoretical framework and advertising appeal themes. Findings The review reveals a transition from traditional rational-emotional appeals toward integrated sustainable, digital, influencer and identity-based communication. Green and corporate social responsibility appeals emerged after 2010, whereas digital and influencer-based persuasion has been gaining prominence since 2015. Emotional and social appeals tend to produce more persuasive results compared with rational appeals, depending on such factors as credibility, authenticity, culture, generations, consumer identity and communication context. Practical implications The results will assist marketing experts, policymakers and communication strategists in creating context-based, credible, authentic and emotional campaigns aimed at promoting socially responsible behavior. Originality/value This review provides an analysis of fragmented literature on advertising appeals by applying the SRC approach, which highlights the idea that no single appeal is universally effective. latest.title: A Theoretical Study on the Conceptual Integration of Plasticity and Resilience in Lifespan Developmental Psychology
latest.venue: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Over decades, lifespan developmental psychology has gradually developed a research paradigm centered on the entire life course. Within this framework, "plasticity" and "resilience" have emerged as two key concepts, each reflecting human development from different perspectives—plasticity emphasizing changeability and adaptability, while resilience highlighting stability and stress resistance. However, for a long time, these two constructs have often been studied separately in both theoretical construction and empirical research: plasticity primarily focuses on the potential and extent of changes in cognition, emotion, and behavior due to internal or external influences, underscoring openness and malleability in development; resilience, by contrast, examines individuals' capacity to maintain or restore optimal functioning after facing adversity, setbacks, or stress, emphasizing developmental stability and coping strength. This separation has limited the explanatory power of existing theories, making it difficult to fully account for the coexistence of change and continuity, vulnerability and strength throughout development. This article, grounded in the holistic perspective of lifespan developmental psychology, reviews the origins, meanings, and applications of plasticity and resilience in lifespan research, and compares their similarities and differences in theoretical assumptions, research methods, and measurement tools. It argues for the possibility and necessity of integrating these two concepts. The paper contends that plasticity serves as a prerequisite for resilience—what people demonstrate as resilience in times of hardship is essentially a manifestation of plasticity under specific conditions. latest.title: The Psychological Mechanisms of Scarcity Marketing on Gen Z Impulse Buying Behavior in Malaysia: A Conceptual Framework
latest.abstract: Scarcity marketing has become a dominant persuasive strategy in digital retail, yet its psychological impact on Generation Z consumers in Malaysia remains underexplored. This concept paper proposes a conceptual framework examining the psychological mechanisms through which scarcity marketing influences impulse buying behavior among Malaysian Gen Z consumers. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and integrating Commodity Theory and Social Comparison Theory, the framework posits that three scarcity marketing stimuli—time-limited, quantity-limited, and social proof scarcity—activate four psychological mediators: fear of missing out (FOMO), competitive arousal, perceived urgency, and social comparison, which subsequently drive impulse buying behavior. The framework further proposes that self-control, digital literacy, financial literacy, and brand trust moderate these relationships. Drawing upon a systematic review of literature from 2017 to 2026, this paper synthesizes empirical evidence demonstrating that FOMO exerts the strongest mediating influence on impulse buying, while self-control consistently weakens the relationship between psychological mediators and behavioral outcomes. The proposed framework contributes to consumer behavior theory by clarifying the mediating pathways and boundary conditions of scarcity marketing effects and offers practical implications for marketers, policymakers and consumer educators in developing responsible marketing practices and targeted digital literacy interventions. Empirical validation through quantitative survey methods targeting 400 Malaysian Gen Z consumers aged 18–27 is proposed to test the hypothesized relationships using Structural Equation Modelling.

latest.title: Gamification in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Engagement and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In the contemporary digital marketplace, consumer attention has become increasingly fragmented due to information overload and constant exposure to competing stimuli. Traditional marketing strategies often fail to sustain meaningful engagement, necessitating innovative approaches that integrate motivational design with experiential value. This paper proposes the Gamified Experiential Marketing Framework (GEMF), a novel conceptual model that unites gamification mechanics with experiential marketing principles to address declining consumer attention and foster sustainable brand loyalty. Drawing upon Self-Determination Theory, Flow Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, GEMF explains how gamification elements such as points, badges, leaderboards, and narratives activate psychological mediators of motivation, experiential value, and emotional engagement. These mediators, moderated by contextual factors including platform characteristics, cultural context, and demographics, lead to enhanced consumer engagement, loyalty, and immersive brand experiences. The paper contributes theoretically by bridging gamification and experiential marketing, offering a holistic framework that positions gamification as a motivational engine within digital marketing. Practically, GEMF provides actionable insights for marketers to design personalized, ethical, and technologically integrated campaigns. Recommendations for future research include longitudinal studies, cross-cultural validation, and exploration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and augmented reality. By situating gamification within experiential marketing, GEMF advances both academic discourse and managerial practice, offering a pathway to reimagine consumer-brand relationships in an era of attention sca

latest.title: Marketing Communication Strategy Through Social Media Content based on Local Wisdom to Increase the Added Value of Indonesian Coffee Brands (Study on Conservation Coffee Brands Based on Local Wisdom)
latest.abstract: The coffee industry is a significant sector in Indonesia, contributing to both domestic production and consumption. However, challenges such as declining production due to climate change, limited agricultural land, and increasing global competition have encouraged coffee businesses to adopt more innovative marketing strategies. One emerging approach involves social media marketing communications that incorporate local cultural values and traditional knowledge. This study aimed to explore the social media marketing communication strategies employed by Indonesian coffee businesses, particularly those incorporating local wisdom, and examine their implications for brand value. A descriptive qualitative approach employing a holistic single-case study design was adopted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and coffee business owners who actively incorporated local wisdom-based content into their marketing strategies. The findings indicated that such content fostered emotional connections with consumers, enhanced brand awareness and engagement, and strengthened brand loyalty. These findings highlight the strategic potential of integrating local cultural values into social media marketing communications to enhance brand differentiation, strengthen perceived brand value, and support long-term business sustainability in Indonesia's coffee industry

latest.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical researc

latest.title: Ethical Consumerism and Identity Construction in Bangladeshi Advertising
latest.abstract: This study looks at the production of an ethical consumer subjectivity in Bangladesh and argues that a distinctive pious consumer culture is constructed, linking both global Islamic laws and local cultural practices. Examining interview-based data of 50 Bangladeshi advertisers from a cultural studies perspective, this paper demonstrates how Islamic cues around ethical consumption narratives work through advertising to sustain a neoliberal logic of global capitalism in the country. It offers an understanding of the emergence of Islamic cultural texts through an interaction among culture, consumption, religion, advertising, and neoliberal capitalism. The ambivalent position of Bangladeshi advertisers in upholding an Islamic identity is also the focal point of this study. Philosophy and Progress, Vol#77-78; No#1-2; Jan-Dec 2025 P 243-280

latest.title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
latest.venue: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
latest.abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

latest.title: Brand Image, e-WoM, and Hedonic Motivation in GTA V Purchase Decisions among Indonesian Generation Z
latest.abstract: more than a decade after its initial release, making it a useful legacy-game context for examining how brand perceptions, consumer-generated digital information, and enjoyment-related motives are associated with purchase decisions among Indonesian Generation Z consumers. Objective: This study examines the associations of brand image, electronic word of mouth (e-WoM), and hedonic motivation with GTA V purchase decisions among Generation Z in Indonesia. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative survey was administered online to 250 respondents recruited through purposive sampling. The four constructs were measured with 16 indicators on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26. Results: Brand image (B = 0.285, t = 4.215, p < 0.001), e-WoM (B = 0.312, t = 4.682, p < 0.001), and hedonic motivation (B = 0.364, t = 5.841, p < 0.001) were each positively associated with purchase decision. The model was significant (F = 130.421, p < 0.001) and explained 61.4% of the variance based on adjusted R². Conclusion: Purchase decisions for this legacy video game are statistically associated with brand-related perceptions, digital consumer communication, and hedonic motives. Because the reported coefficients are unstandardized and the design is cross-sectional, the findings do not establish relative dominance or causality.

latest.title: Decoding anthropomorphism: a multidimensional perspective on presence, parasocial relationship and purchase intention
latest.abstract: Abstract Virtual influencers have become an increasingly important marketing tool, yet existing research has offered limited insight into how their anthropomorphic attributes should be conceptualized and through which psychological mechanisms they influence consumer responses. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes virtual influencer anthropomorphism as a multidimensional construct consisting of physical anthropomorphism, interactivity intelligence, and mental human-likeness, and examines its effects on purchase intention through social presence, telepresence, and parasocial relationship. Using online survey data, the results show that all three anthropomorphic attributes positively enhance consumers’ social presence and telepresence, which in turn strengthen parasocial relationships and subsequently increase purchase intention. The findings further refine the conceptualization of virtual influencer anthropomorphism by highlighting the importance of interaction-based anthropomorphism alongside visual and mental human-like cues. Overall, this study contributes to the literature by clarifying both the multidimensional nature of virtual influencer anthropomorphism and the psychological process through which it shapes consumer behavior.

latest.title: The psychology of AI-driven virtual endorsement: How narrative transportation shapes consumer engagement, brand perceptions, and purchase intentions among Gen-Z in Pakistan
latest.abstract: Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI)-created virtual influencers are revolutionizing influencer marketing, but little is known about how their attributes relate to positive consumer reactions. Current studies have focused primarily on measures of engagement and credibility of the narrator and ignored the effect of immersive storytelling on the perceived endorsed brand. This study examines the effect of anthropomorphism, perceived authenticity and perceived similarity on the brand credibility, consumer engagement and purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in an emerging market, based on Narrative Transportation Theory. Design/methodology/approach: A quantitative, cross sectional study was conducted with 400 samples of Generation Z university students in Pakistan. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to analyze data to explore the direct and indirect relationships. Results: The findings show that narrative transportation is the most important psychological mechanism that influences the consumer response to the characteristics of the virtual influencers. Both perceived authenticity and perceived similarity contribute to consumers' immersion in the virtual influencer's stories, which positively affects brand credibility, and thereby boosts consumer engagement and purchase intention. However, the unexpected negative effect of anthropomorphism on narrative transportation indicates that if too human-like, anthropomorphism can be detrimental to persuasive processing when using AI in influencer marketing. Originality/value: The study contributes to the existing knowledge on influencer marketing by applying the Narrative Transportation Theory to the virtual influencer context and by it assessing the role of immersive narrative experience

latest.title: MARCAS ESPORTIVAS E CONSTRUÇÃO DA IDENTIDADE DO CONSUMIDOR: RELAÇÕES ENTRE BRANDING, VALORES E ESTILOS DE VIDA
latest.abstract: O artigo examina de que maneira a literatura científica sobre branding articula valores, estilos de vida e significados simbólicos na construção da identidade do consumidor de marcas esportivas. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa, com busca realizada no Google Acadêmico a partir da pergunta de pesquisa e dos termos que compõem o título, da qual resultou um corpus principal de oito artigos publicados em periódicos científicos, complementado por sete fontes de apoio conceitual, entre teses, dissertações, projeto profissional de mestrado e livro. Os estudos foram analisados por meio de matriz de extração e de síntese comparativa organizada em três categorias: identificação com a marca e congruência identitária; herança e autenticidade; comunicação e construção de significados. Os resultados indicam que a identificação com marcas é um fenômeno multidimensional e contextual, sensível à congruência com o estilo de vida, ao prestígio percebido e à convergência de valores, mas não equivale a lealdade, defesa da marca ou reconhecimento visual. A herança e a autenticidade contribuem para a densidade simbólica das marcas por vias distintas e, em geral, mediadas pela experiência estética e pela reinterpretação narrativa do passado. Verificou-se, ainda, que esses eixos vêm sendo investigados de forma predominantemente independente, o que confere valor teórico à integração proposta e orienta uma agenda de pesquisa para o setor esportivo. Conclui-se que as marcas esportivas operam como recursos simbólicos de expressão identitária, cuja eficácia depende da coerência entre o que a marca projeta e aquilo que o consumidor reconhece como próprio.

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: Transparency matters
latest.abstract: This study examines how sponsorship disclosure format and influencer compensation nature shape perceived sponsorship transparency and its effects on source credibility, information credibility, online engagement, and purchase intention among Instagram micro-influencers. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model, Communication Transparency Theory, Parasocial Interaction Theory, and Source Credibility Theory, the study conceptualizes perceived sponsorship transparency as consumers’ holistic judgment of how openly the commercial relationship is communicated. A between-subjects experiment (420 participants) was analyzed using two-way analysis of variance, regression, and serial mediation. Disclosure format, but not compensation nature, influenced perceived transparency, with platform-integrated disclosures outperforming hashtag-based ones, extending the Persuasion Knowledge Model to platform-governed ecosystems. Transparency sequentially mediated behavioral outcomes through source and information credibility, with source credibility the stronger mediator. Limitations include snowball sampling, a fictitious influencer and brand, and no confirmatory factor analysis.

latest.title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Findings Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. Originality/value The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across natio

latest.title: Modeling the Brand Strength Component in Monetary Brand Valuation Using Fuzzy Logic: Evidence From a Place Brand
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose : Monetary brand valuation remains a persistent challenge in brand management, due to the absence of transparent approaches for operationalizing brand strength. While financial-based valuation methods are well established, the integration of perceptual and behavioral dimensions into monetary frameworks remains limited. The purpose of this study is to develop and test a methodological approach for modeling the Brand Strength component within monetary brand valuation. The approach is operationalized as an interpretable fuzzy inference model that integrates perceptual data, objective indicators, and expert knowledge. The case of Ülemiste City in Tallinn, Estonia, is used as an empirical example to demonstrate and test the approach’s practical applicability. Design/methodology/approach : The study proposes a fuzzy framework for estimating brand strength in monetary brand valuation. The approach integrates heterogeneous data sources, including survey-based perceptions, objective indicators, and expert knowledge, within a rule-based, interpretable model. The model is empirically demonstrated through an application to the Ülemiste City place brand. Findings : The results show that this model produces consistent, interpretable brand-strength coefficients and supports two complementary use cases: internal, target-based brand management and cross-brand comparability. The findings demonstrate that fuzzy logic provides a practical mechanism for combining diverse sources of brand-related information into a coherent monetary valuation framework. Originality/value : This study advances brand management by offering a transparent method for integrating brand strength into monetary valuation, linking financial metrics with perception-based assessments. Given the lack of

latest.title: When Does Sustainable Storytelling Foster Advocacy Intention? The Mediating Roles of Perceived ESG Authenticity and Emotional Brand Resonance, and the Moderating Role of Green Scepticism in Digital Ecosystems
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Amid widespread greenwashing and consumer scepticism, brands struggle to convert sustainability commitments into advocacy intention. This study examines sustainable digital storytelling encompassing narrative environmental framing (NEF), interactive sustainability co‐narration (ISC), and temporal impact visualisation (TIV) as a distinct communicative mode. Drawing on narrative transportation, signalling, and attribution theories, we develop a moderated‐mediation model linking these storytelling dimensions to sustainable consumption advocacy intention (SCAI) through perceived ESG authenticity (ESGA) and emotional brand resonance (EBR), with green scepticism (GSCP) as a boundary condition. A three‐wave, time‐lagged survey of 512 Vietnamese consumers confirms that all three storytelling dimensions enhance ESGA and EBR, which in turn predict advocacy intention, with no statistically significant residual direct effects of storytelling on advocacy. However, green scepticism attenuates these effects, diminishing compelling narratives' motivational impact. This study extends narrative transportation theory to the sustainable digital branding domain, identifies a dual cognitive‐affective pathway through which storytelling generates advocacy intention, and establishes green scepticism as a boundary condition that attenuates advocacy conversion even when authenticity and resonance perceptions are strong.

latest.title: Why Does Gamification Fail? The Impact Mechanisms of Gamification Design Flaws on Consumers' Continuous Purchase Intention
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approach to uncover the influence mechanisms of gamification design flaws. In Study 1, we collected 24,749 consumer comments describing negative experiences with gamified shopping festivals. By combining BERTopic modeling with a human‐LLM collaboration, we identified seven latent concepts. Further analysis grounded in psychological reactance theory and affective events theory indicated that four gamification design flaws, namely narrative rhythm disruption, game interaction complexity, reward value distortion, and gameplay replaceability, affect consumers' continuous purchase intention through perceived manipulation and frustration. In Study 2, we collected survey responses from 398 consumers who participated in the gamified shopping festivals and used PLS‐SEM to test the proposed hypotheses. This research deepens understanding of the adverse side of gamification, contributes to theoretical perspectives on the mechanisms of gamification design flaws, and provides novel insights for optimizing gamification in e‐commerce platforms.

latest.title: Religiosity and consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z: does gender make a difference?
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how religiosity is associated with consumer behaviour among Millennials and Gen Z in a highly religious emerging market. It proposes the spiritual cognitive consumption theory (SCCT), a dual pathway framework, and provides preliminary empirical support for its overall predictive validity. However, these two pathways were not directly measured; future experimental research is needed to isolate each mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 400 Nigerian respondents were analysed using structural equation modelling. Gender significantly moderates this relationship: women tend to show a stronger association between religiosity and relational aspects (e.g. brand trust, emotional congruity), whereas men focus more on instrumental outcomes (e.g. product functionality, religious symbolism). Findings The SCCT framework provides a nuanced understanding of the tension between spiritual devotion and market-based consumption. The findings offer marketers gender-sensitive, faith-conscious strategies and position SCCT as a robust theoretical tool for understanding spirituality, cognition and consumption in evolving digital economies. Social implications The study contributes to sustainable development goal (SDG) 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) by providing insights into inclusive, faith-sensitive marketing practices in the Global South. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in the development of the SCCT framework, which integrates spirituality, cognition and consumption into a dual pathway model. This offers a novel theoretical lens for understanding consumer behaviour in religious emerging markets.

latest.title: Parasocial relationships in informal digital beauty education: explainable machine learning evidence from YouTube beauty influencers
latest.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
latest.abstract: Social media beauty influencers increasingly function as informal sources of procedural, product, and aesthetic knowledge, yet the relational mechanisms connecting audiences to these digital sources remain underexplored. This study examines parasocial relationship (PSR) strength in the Beauty & Fashion subset of a multimodal YouTube influencer dataset and introduces RAPID-PSR, a relational-aware, pseudo-labeled, interpretable ordinal ensemble framework. The dataset comprised 3,329 observations, including 819 usable human-annotated cases categorized as absent, weak, moderate, or strong PSR, and 2,483 application observations. RAPID-PSR combines behavioral and creator-context variables, engineered relational features, TF-IDF-based text representations, cumulative ordinal learning, an adaptive XGBoost-LightGBM-CatBoost ensemble, confidence-based pseudo-labeling, and ordinal SHAP explanations. An independent test partition (n = 158) was retained for evaluation. RAPID-PSR achieved 66.46% accuracy, macro-F1 = 0.553, quadratic weighted kappa = 0.647, ordinal MAE = 0.380, macro ROC-AUC = 0.810, and macro PR-AUC = 0.590. It produced the highest accuracy, macro-F1, QWK, and lowest ordinal error, while CatBoost achieved the strongest ROC-AUC and log-loss performance. SHAP analysis identified textual semantics, interaction depth, reciprocal engagement, interaction regularity, relational warmth, and sentiment as major predictors of PSR strength. Survey-linked validation further showed substantial convergence between computational and self-reported PSR scores (Pearson r = 0.666; Spearman ρ = 0.644). The findings highlight relational continuity and responsive interaction as important signals in creator-led informal beauty learning while emphasizing the distinction between interpersona

latest.title: Human-Centered Marketing 5.0 Practices and Consumer Trust among University Students in Klang Valley
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: The study examined the relationship between human-centered Marketing 5.0 practices and consumer trust among university students in Klang Valley, Malaysia. It was grounded in Marketing 5.0 as the primary framework and guided by the Technology Acceptance Model and Commitment-Trust Theory, with a particular emphasis on predictive, contextual and augmented marketing as consumer-oriented applications of AI. The data were collected through a quantitative, cross-sectional survey using convenience and purposive sampling to get 200 usable responses from the university students aged 18-29 who have experience in digital-platform or online-transaction. The data were gathered by a self-administered online questionnaire with 20 measurement items on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Consumer trust was significantly positively related to all three practices. The standardized contribution (?) was highest for augmented marketing (? = .371, p < .001), followed by contextual marketing (? = .352, p < .001) and predictive marketing (? = .141, p = .022). The three predictors accounted for 60.9% of the variance in consumer trust (R² = .609). The results of predictive and contextual marketing should be interpreted with caution as these measures had lower internal consistency and factor suitability. The results offer actionable insights for companies aiming to create clear, meaningful, and responsive AI-driven marketing strategies that support consumer trust.

latest.title: Building consumer–brand relationships in omni-channel retailing: AI personalization, relationship marketing, satisfaction, trust, and data privacy concerns
latest.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming customer relationship management by enabling personalized and seamless interactions across multiple channels. However, it remains unclear whether AI-based personalization can build customer relationships as effectively as traditional relationship marketing. This study examines the effects of AI-Driven Personalization (AIDP) and Traditional Relationship Marketing (TRM) on Customer Retention (CR), while exploring the mediating roles of Customer Satisfaction (CS) and Customer Trust (CT) and the moderating role of Data Privacy Concerns (DPC). Using a positivist philosophy and deductive approach, data were collected from 407 Omni-channel customers in Pakistan and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings show that both AIDP and TRM significantly enhance customer satisfaction and trust, which subsequently strengthen retention. Customer satisfaction also positively influences trust, while trust emerges as the strongest predictor of retention. Moreover, Data Privacy Concerns significantly moderate the trust–retention relationship, demonstrating that customers’ perceptions of how their personal information is handled can shape their trust. The study integrates technological and relational approaches within relationship marketing theory in an Omni-channel context.

latest.title: The Influence of Customer Experience, Brand Love, and Customer Satisfaction on Customer Loyalty
latest.abstract: Customer loyalty is an important determinant of business sustainability and competitive advantage in increasingly competitive markets. Understanding the factors that encourage customers to maintain long-term relationships with brands is therefore essential for effective marketing management. This study aims to examine the influence of customer experience, brand love, and customer satisfaction on customer loyalty. A quantitative research approach with an explanatory design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire to collect data from customers who have purchased or used the products or services of a selected brand. The proposed analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement reliability and validity and examine the relationships among the research constructs. The results indicate that customer experience, brand love, and customer satisfaction are positively associated with customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction demonstrating the largest estimated path coefficient, followed by brand love and customer experience. These findings suggest that businesses may strengthen customer loyalty by creating positive customer experiences, fostering emotional attachment to their brands, and consistently meeting customer expectations. The study contributes to the marketing literature by integrating experiential, emotional, and evaluative perspectives into a single framework for understanding customer loyalty.

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: Experiential branding in the digital age: evaluative and experiential pathways from brand experience to customer satisfaction
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines the psychological mechanisms linking brand experience and customer satisfaction. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework and appraisal theory, it investigates the mediating roles of brand authenticity and brand engagement, treated, respectively, as an evaluative (cognitive-appraisal) and a multidimensional experiential-investment organismic pathway. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 304 smartphone consumers in Haryana NCR (India) using a structured questionnaire and a non-probability convenience sample. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4) was used to test the model, which incorporates two reflective higher-order constructs and two mediators modelled in parallel (a formative Mode B re-estimation of the higher-order constructs, a sensitivity analysis with and without one affection item and a bootstrap contrast of the two specific indirect effects were added as robustness checks and a formal comparison). One indicator (AFFBENG3; loading 0.376) was removed post hoc; the structural results are the same when it is retained. Findings Brand experience is positively related to customer satisfaction, brand authenticity and brand engagement. Brand engagement ( β = 0.424) and brand authenticity ( β = 0.128) are both positively related to satisfaction, with engagement showing the numerically larger coefficient. Both specific indirect effects are significant (through engagement β = 0.107; through authenticity β = 0.048) alongside a significant direct path (β = 0.136), a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation through two mediators modelled in parallel; because the direct path is small, this classification is treated cautiously. A bootstrap contrast showed

latest.title: AI-Enabled Hospitality Services and Consumer Repurchase Intention: The Roles of Technology Readiness, Technological Empowerment, Emotional Attachment, and Trust
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: This study investigates how technology adoption propensity (TAP) is associated with consumers’ intention to repurchase AI-enabled hospitality services by examining the mediating roles of perceived technological empowerment (PTE) and brand emotional attachment (BEA), as well as the moderating role of trust in AI (TAI). Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework and the technology readiness perspective, cross-sectional survey data were collected from 439 guests of deluxe hotels in Greater Cairo, Egypt, and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that TAP is positively associated with both PTE and BEA. PTE is positively associated with BEA and partially mediates the TAP–BEA association, and the sequential indirect association between TAP and repurchase intention through PTE and BEA is significant. BEA emerges as a strong predictor of repurchase intention, while TAI strengthens the relationship between BEA and repurchase intention. The study contributes by showing that a general technology predisposition is linked to post-adoption repurchase intentions through a cognitive-to-affective chain (empowerment, then brand attachment) while retaining a larger direct link to attachment, and by identifying trust in AI as a boundary condition of the attachment–intention link. Because the design is cross-sectional and measures intentions, the results indicate associations rather than causal effects.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER PURCHASING DECISIONS.
authors: Caroline Dias da Silva de Carvalho
latest.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the impact of digital marketing and digital influencers on consumer behavior. The methodology used comprised the following research methods: in the first phase, a bibliographic review was conducted in order to analyze, in the scientific literature, the transformation from traditional marketing to digital marketing, as well as the role of social media and digital influencers in purchase decisions; in the second stage, a field research was carried out through the application of a structured questionnaire, aiming to identify consumers' perceptions regarding the influence exerted by these agents on their consumption habits. The results obtained indicated that digital marketing significantly influenced consumer behavior, making consumers more active and informed, while digital influencers exerted a strong impact on opinion formation and purchase decisions, especially due to the credibility and identification established with the audience. It was concluded that digital marketing and digital influencers played an essential role in contemporary business strategies, being fundamental for building relationships with consumers and strengthening brands in the digital environment.

latest.title: Identificação da utilização do método hipotético-dedutivo nos estudos de Destination Branding na base de dados Hospitality & Tourism Complete – EBSCOhost
latest.venue: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade
latest.abstract: A teoria do destination branding tem sido amplamente utilizada para investigar marcas de destinos turísticos, consolidados ou emergentes. Sua natureza abrangente permite avaliar constructos essenciais para compreender a representação do destino e sua competitividade no mercado. A marca, ao comunicar atributos culturais, sociais e experienciais, torna-se um instrumento estratégico na diferenciação territorial e no fortalecimento da atratividade turística. Este estudo tem como objetivo identificar o uso do método hipotético-dedutivo em artigos alinhados à perspectiva neopositivista, disponíveis na base Hospitality & Tourism Complete – EBSCOhost. Adotou-se uma abordagem qualitativa, de caráter exploratório, utilizando o levantamento bibliométrico. A busca inicial resultou na identificação de 232 artigos por meio das palavras-chave “destination”, “branding” e “management”. A triagem realizada no software Excel permitiu selecionar os estudos que abordavam especificamente o destination branding, resultando em 54 artigos, dos quais 14 empregavam o método hipotético-dedutivo. Os resultados evidenciam que o destination branding desempenha papel relevante na construção da imagem de destino e na consolidação de estratégias de marketing territorial. As tendências de pesquisa observadas reforçam a importância de modelos teóricos que permitam mensurar variáveis relacionadas à marca, contribuindo para avanços teóricos e práticos. Nos estudos analisados, as abordagens neopositivistas sustentadas pelo método hipotético-dedutivo demonstram potencial para aprimorar a gestão turística, uma vez que permitem testar hipóteses, identificar relações causais e fortalecer a compreensão dos constructos que influenciam o desempenho das marcas destino. Observa-se que o destination branding permanece

latest.title: The influence of AI chatbots’ human-like and technical characteristics on users’ perceived addictiveness
latest.abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative AI chatbots, their human-like and technical characteristics may enhance user experience while also increasing the risks of overdependence and potential addiction. However, how these two categories of characteristics jointly shape users’ perceived addictiveness remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, this study developed a model integrating perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, emotional attachment, functional dependence, and perceived addictiveness. Data were collected from 345 Chinese AI chatbot users through an online survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use all positively influenced trust, which in turn strengthened emotional attachment and functional dependence. Both emotional attachment and functional dependence increased perceived addictiveness, with emotional attachment exerting the stronger effect. Mediation analysis further indicated that chatbot characteristics indirectly influenced perceived addictiveness through two parallel pathways: trust–emotional attachment and trust–functional dependence. These findings reveal the emotional and functional mechanisms underlying perceived AI chatbot addictiveness, extend the S–O–R framework, and provide implications for responsible design, calibrated trust, and dependence-risk governance.

latest.title: Authenticity in marketing: A conceptual model and meta-analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
